picks.headline: Staff predictions for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt: Can the Hokies start 5-0?
picks.blurb: BLACKSBURG, Va. — Virginia Tech football takes on Pitt tomorrow night in its fifth contest of the 2026 season. Ahead of the Friday evening clash against the Panthers, three members of our staff offered their thoughts on what could unfold tomorrow: JACKSON CAUDELL: This is the biggest Virginia Tech game in years. If they win, they will be 5-0 and have a win against one of the teams expected to compete for a spot in the ACC Championship game, giving them a huge tiebreaker. You could argue that the winner of this game is going to be in the best position to make it to Charlotte and likely face Miami . I expect this to be a close game, but the home-field advantage and Virginia Tech's defense are going to be the difference. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 20 JAMES DUNCAN: Nobody has scored on Pitt in the first or third quarter this season. The Panthers allow 8.5 points per game, fewest in the ACC. Against a Virginia Tech line missing left tackle Justin Terry, I don't see the Hokies hanging 40. Expect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer to live on quick throws to tight end Luke Reynolds. But Pitt has been flagged 37 times for 359 yards, all at home. Now its first road trip is Lane Stadium on a Friday night. If pre-snap penalties have been an issue at home, who knows what it will be in front of 65,000 people screaming at the top of their lungs when trying to hear a snap count. I still expect this game to come down to the final snap. In fact, I’m predicting a walk-off field goal from John Love to give James Franklin his signature moment in his first season at Virginia Tech. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 21 THOMAS HUGHES: Virginia Tech has an opportunity to turn a promising start into a true renaissance Friday night. Pitt presents a challenge on defense, and the Hokies will need to help Ethan Grunkemeyer avoid spending the evening under pressure. Quick throws to Luke Reynolds and a productive rushing attack should be central to that effort, and they should be more available than in last Saturday's rainy affair in Chestnut Hill. Still, I trust Virginia Tech to find enough offense to keep this game within reach throughout. The bigger question is whether the Hokies can force Pitt into the mistakes that become increasingly costly in a close conference matchup. Lane Stadium should have something to say about that, particularly if the Panthers struggle with penalties. I expect a competitive game that remains undecided into the fourth quarter, but that Virginia Tech’s defense delivers the final stop to keep James Franklin’s team unbeaten and firmly in the ACC conversation. picks.headline: Full game preview and score prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt
picks.blurb: BLACKSBURG, Va. — For the first time in 20 days, Virginia Tech football hosts a game at Lane Stadium — this one against Pitt with a 5-0 start hanging in the balance. Both the Hokies (4-0, 1-0 ACC) and Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) enter Friday night's contest with unblemished marks, making the matchup one of four games nationally this week between undefeated FBS teams. For Virginia Tech, a victory would secure its first 5-0 start since 2005 and continue a remarkable turnaround in James Franklin's first season at the helm. Virginia Tech's perfect record hasn't come without adversity. After opening the season with commanding victories over VMI (73-3) and Old Dominion (44-21), the Hokies survived consecutive road tests against Maryland and Boston College . Tech defeated the Terrapins 35-26 before escaping a rain-soaked Chestnut Hill with a 21-14 victory. The latter required Virginia Tech to overcome a 14-6 fourth-quarter deficit. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 14-yard score to Marlion Jackson, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. broke free for a 76-yard touchdown less than three minutes later to put the Hokies ahead for good. Overton's emergence has added another dimension to an offense that relied heavily on Grunkemeyer through the first three weeks. The sophomore enters Friday with 409 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 60 carries, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt. He erupted for a career-high 209 yards on 25 carries against Boston College, earning ACC Running Back of the Week honors. Finding similar success against Pitt, though, will be difficult. The Panthers enter Blacksburg allowing just 53.3 rushing yards per game and 8.5 points per contest. Pitt's defense has surrendered just 34 points through four games, following a 59-14 win over Miami (Ohio) with victories of 12-7 over UCF, 27-13 over Syracuse and 59-0 over Bucknell. That creates perhaps the game's most important matchup. Virginia Tech has found a potential difference-maker in Overton, but Pitt possesses one of the stingiest rushing defenses in the country. If the Panthers can prevent Overton from consistently reaching the second level, more responsibility will fall back onto Grunkemeyer. The Penn State transfer has largely handled that responsibility well. Grunkemeyer has completed 101 of 136 passes for 1,012 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Boston College limited him to 147 passing yards, but the weather played a significant factor. Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel has completed 88 of 130 passes for 1,191 yards, 13 touchdowns and just one interception. His season began with a historic seven-touchdown performance against Miami (Ohio), and he threw for 403 yards and six touchdowns in last week's demolition of Bucknell. Heintschel became the first ACC quarterback to record multiple six-touchdown passing games in the same season. That should provide Virginia Tech's pass rush with its biggest challenge yet. The Hokies have consistently disrupted opposing backfields, entering Friday averaging 4.25 sacks and 11.3 tackles for loss per game. Cortez Harris has led that charge with five sacks, including two in the victory over Boston College. Getting to Heintschel could be critical. Pitt averages 347.3 passing yards and 39.3 points per game, and its passing attack isn't dependent on a single target. Thirteen different Panthers caught a pass against Bucknell, while five players hauled in touchdowns. Censere Lee led the scoring barrage with three touchdown receptions. Friday also represents something Pitt hasn't experienced this season: a road game. The Panthers played each of their first four contests at Acrisure Stadium and now head into a sold-out Lane Stadium for a primetime matchup. Pitt is 3-8 all-time in Blacksburg, although the Panthers have won three of the last four overall meetings between the programs. Virginia Tech won the most recent matchup, 38-21, in 2023. Virginia Tech has answered four different tests through four weeks. Pitt presents another, and perhaps the most complete one yet. One undefeated record will disappear Friday night. Which one do I think will? Virginia Tech's defense should give Pitt its toughest test yet, while Lane Stadium could make the Panthers' first road game uncomfortable. The Hokies may not completely contain Heintschel, but Overton and Grunkemeyer should generate enough offense late to preserve the unbeaten start in a tightly contested ACC matchup. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech final odds and prediction for Week 5 vs. Pittsburgh Skip to main content About Virginia Tech Hokies News Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Hokies In the NFL Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball After the Virginia Tech and Pittsburgh football teams have begun the season perfectly at 4-0, the two will face off on Friday night at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg in a massive primetime showdown that will have a lot of eyes on it. When the ball is kicked off, the two teams will make history as the only two undefeated Power 4 teams to meet this late in the season without either team being ranked . Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin and Pitt coach Pat Narduzzi don't care about that and are just focusing on winning the game. Whoever wins the game should be ranked in Sunday's Associated Press Top 25 poll. Let's take a look at the latest odds and make a prediction for the biggest game in almost a decade in Blacksburg. Virginia Tech vs. Boston College: Final odds, spread, and total Odds provided by DraftKings Sportsbook Virginia Tech (-162) Pittsburgh (+136) Virginia Tech -2.5 (-115) Pittsburgh +2.5 (-105) 54.5 (over -118/under -102) Virginia Tech vs. Pittsburgh Prediction This is an interesting matchup. This is Pittsburgh's first true road game of the season, as the first four games they have played have been at home against Miami of Ohio, Central Florida, Syracuse, and Bucknell. The Hokies have won home games against VMI and Old Dominion, as well as road games the last two weeks at Maryland and Boston College. The latter was played in a Nor'easter and required a fourth-quarter rally to remain undefeated. This is a matchup between two teams that have proven to have explosive offenses with young and talented quarterbacks. The question is going to come down to the defenses. Which unit will create more turnovers? Will Pitt's defensive line be a problem for Virginia Tech's patchwork offensive line? Will the Hokies' crowd affect the Panthers' offense, which is on the road for the first time in 2026? So many questions will be answered that will have an effect on the outcome. In the end, this is a complete toss-up, but the Hokies secondary has been struggling this season, and with Panthers QB Mason Heintschel, if he gets into a rhythm, it could be a long night for Brent Pry's crew. Going with the gut, not the heart. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. Pittsburgh Panthers: News, Updates, and Predictions | Gobbler Country Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Virginia Tech Hokies Community Gobbler Country October 2, 2026 Gobbler Country Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech Basketball Virginia Tech Baseball Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Virginia Tech Football Odds Virginia Tech Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Virginia Tech Football Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech hosts the Pittsburgh Panthers in an old fashioned Big East grudge match. Tech is a narrow homefield favorite, but the media and commentariat don’t agree. It’s looking like a season where the upcoming game is the most important game of the season. If you had to pick a really obvious one out of the stack, the Pitt game runs right to the top of the flagpole. Let’s look at some team news, a few updates here and there, and then get to the predictions. It’s not Homecoming, but It is Stripe Lane Night The program has fan gimmicks for most games this season, and it’s a night where certain sections wear orange, and others wear maroon. Sometimes it works out, and sometimes it sort of looks like more than half the people didn’t care or didn’t know. Just a Reminder that the Team in Maroon Earned Its Way Last Saturday in a New England coastal Nor’easter, the Hokies earned their respect the hard way, by fighting BC and the weather to catch, pass, and then burn out the clock before they had a chance to respond. Jeffrey Overton, Jr. Gets Some Kudos He gets named ACC Running Back of the Week for his powerful performance in the rain and wind of Alumni Stadium. PFF picks out Overton but also adds Quentin Reddish and Jaquez White for their National Team of the Week notice. Catch Up with Coach Franklin’s Weekly Presser This is nearly a 51-minute watch so go grab a coffee. Lots of good information in this one. Predictions Time Huge game for the Hokies. This game means a lot for several reasons. A chance to go 5-0, a chance to go 2-0 in the ACC, a chance to re-establish Lane Stadium as a place that visiting teams dread coming to play. Pitt is a tough challenge. Under Pat Narduzzi, the Panthers always play a tough brand of football. They generally play solid defense and rely on the running game. They now have a quarterback who can air it out. Pitt’s strengths and Virginia Tech’s potential weaknesses match up well for the Panthers. The Hokies have allowed some big plays through the air this year, so Pitt will test that. I have concerns about Pitt’s run defense. The Hokies have had some issues at times this year and are dealing with multiple injuries along the offensive line. That’s something to watch. I do think the Hokies will make some plays in the running game. More Jeffrey Overton, please. Luke Reynolds had a down game last week, due to the weather more than anything, but I expect a big bounce-back this week. Reynolds catches another touchdown and quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer is the better quarterback on the field again this week. It’s close, but the Hokies win. Virginia Tech 27, Pitt 21 Tough games require some tough thinking. This one is essentially a toss-up, and regardless of these two teams’ records they always seem to be a fist fight street brawl. This season neither team is ranked, but neither is showing up at Lane Stadium with a loss on their record. Tech is rallying up behind a completely revamped and very different offense than we have seen since the Michael Brewer days at the end of the Beamer Era. This Tech team has an actual quarterback, uses its tight ends and gets downfield with intermediate distance pass plays. The defensive style isn’t much different than has been fielded in the past, but the line is bigger and a bit faster than we are used to. It still has problems with running quarterbacks, and the secondary has just not stiffened yet. That’s a concern for this one because Nardo has found a good quarterback, too, and as we saw in the recent past when he has a good quarterback his teams go from wobbly to competitive. To win this Tech has to drive and score on nearly every possession. The defense needs to get fast “A” gap pressure on Pitt’s QB, and the secondary needs to stiffen up considerably. It’s also going to need to avoid any “prevent” situations since Pitt can score fast if it needs to. Add all that stuff up, and this one is going to be one of two things. A runaway with one team dominating over the other with fast offensive and heavy defensive pressure, or both teams are going to force a tough close contest. I am thinking the latter is more likely, I still have pictures in the library of the 4th quarter 4th and Goal for Pitt at the Tech 2. This stacks up to be, in my mind anyway, a similar contest. I think Tech takes it, but it’s going to be close, a 3- or 4-point difference. Both teams are probably good for scores in the mid- to high- twenties. The team that breaks 30 wins. 31 - 24 Hokies Just a Reminder About Friday Evening If you are coming to the game, check your seat against the chart, and wear the appropriate color. We’ll be on the field, cameras going, stay with us for pictures on the Facebook page Saturday evening. GO HOKIES!!!! Skip to main content SI.COM The player availability report, which was first used 2025 season, provides five types of designations: available, probable, questionable, doubtful and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Probable corresponds to "likely to play", offering roughly a 75% chance, per the ACC's explanation. Questionable means "uncertain to play", offering around a 50% chance, while doubtful corresponds to unlikely (25%). Out means the player will not play in the game, while a game-time decision (on game day only) means that the final decision will be made closer to the game itself. It's the second straight week that Virginia Tech has 13 players on the availability report: two are out, nine are questionable and two are probable. Five on the report are wide receivers, while there's five offensive linemen, one running back, one corner and one defensive lineman. First-year head coach James Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore have had to move people around and make adjustments on the fly. That was the case leading into last weekend's battle at Boston College. There was a lot of moving around, and Montavious Cunningham missed the game after suffering an injury last week, but at his weekly press conference on Monday, Franklin sounded like someone who was fairly confident that he might be getting some injured players back against Pittsburgh on Friday night. If that is the case, then it would be a big development against a stout Pitt defensive line. Another key player who missed the Boston College game was wide receiver Ayden Greene. Marlion Jackson filled in for him and hauled in a big fourth-quarter touchdown pass from quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer that tied the game after Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s two-point conversion run. Greene is one of the top receivers for offensive coordinator Ty Howle, and Franklin is also anticipating him to be back on Friday night, per Bitter . home.headline: Virginia Tech football's initial injury report brings both good and bad news
home.blurb: On Tuesday, the initial availability report for the Pitt game was released. Greene and Cunningham were listed as probable, while Terry was listed as out, something that wasn't a surprise after Franklin's comments on Monday . According to David Cunningham of Tech Sideline , Brody Meadows and Cunningham were participants in practice on Tuesday, but did not go through the one-on-ones against the defense. That is a sign that, despite being listed as probable, Cunningham might not go this week against the Panthers either. It's a short week for the Virginia Tech football team after they rallied in the fourth quarter for a 21-14 win last Saturday afternoon at Boston College. Trailing 14-6, the Hokies scored on back-to-back drives late for their first ACC win under James Franklin. The short week means everything moves up a day, including gameday to Friday night, when Virginia Tech hosts Pittsburgh in a battle of two 4-0 teams at Lane Stadium . Franklin and his staff are dealing with some injuries a third of the way through the season, and the initial availability report for Friday night's game was released, and it brought some promising news for the Hokies. Initial availability report brings mixed news for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Last week, the Hokies were thin on offense. The week before, against Maryland, offensive lineman Justin Terry went down with an injury in the second quarter; wide receiver Ayden Greene did, too. Then, before the Hokies flew to Boston, offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham popped up on the injury report. That would be a big loss of a veteran lineman ahead of one of the biggest games in Blacksburg in years. That would force Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore to shuffle more for the game, and likely during it as well. That's less than ideal. As far as Greene goes, it sounds promising that he could play against Pitt, and that would be big for quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer and offensive coordinator Ty Howle. If not, Marlion Jackson should get more reps after he played against BC and hauled in a fourth-quarter touchdown reception that eventually led to a tie game after Jeffrey Overton Jr. added the two-point conversion. There are still a couple more days before kickoff, and the true test will be pregame warmups on Friday night. Coaches want every possible advantage they can get before game day arrives, so handing out information on which of their players could or could not play is somewhat of an immediate disadvantage, because it lets the other team plan accordingly, and personnel is everything in football. In the latest student-athlete availability report for Boston College football's first conference game of the season, which is against Virginia Tech on Saturday in the wake of an impending Nor'easter that could bring heavy winds and sideways rain to Chestnut Hill, Mass., the Eagles have a relatively high number of injuries entering the contest, the majority of which are categorized as fully "out." The players in that category who were just recently injured would be tight ends Brady Clough and Bryce Lewis, defensive back Cameron Martinez, linebackers Bodie Kahoun and Justin Medlock , and defensive tackle Chris Marable Jr., all of whom played in BC's first two games of the year before sitting out against Maine last Saturday. Now in the "doubtful" category is defensive back Syair Torrence, who is slowly making his return from a season-ending injury he sustained just two games into his redshirt-freshman campaign last year. "It's all about health," O'Brien said of the reason he played mostly on special teams. "He's one of our best players. It has nothing to do with anything other than his health. Whether it was coming back from the knee, which was a serious knee injury, or some soft-tissue stuff he's dealing with. But yeah, once he's really 100 percent healthy, he'll [be out there]. He practiced today, so we'll see how it goes for Saturday." On the bright side, defensive end Kris Jones - one of the best pass rushers on the team - is listed as "questionable," and defensive lineman Onye Nwosisi is in the "probably" category. Nwosisi made his season debut last week against Maine and totaled three tackles and two quarterback hits, so his availability is quite massive. The Wildcats turned a fourth-quarter drive into the game-winning touchdown that ended Franklin's tenure as Penn State's head coach. On Friday night, the Nittany Lions get another crack at the Wildcats, this time as part of a grand opening. Northwestern will host Penn State in the first game at the new Ryan Field, a nearly $900 million venue that claims to be the most expensive college stadium ever built. There are plenty of Penn State storylines Friday night beyond a mostly new program getting proxy retribution for last year's loss at Beaver Stadium. More than half of Penn State's roster wasn't on the field that night and doesn't care about settling scores. These Nittany Lions want to settle their offense. With that in mind, here's how we see Friday's Penn State-Northwestern game shaking out, including our predictions from the Penn State on SI staff. Kickoff is scheduled for just after 8 p..m. ET on FOX. 1. Penn State gets a prime bounce-back spot Friday night, laying 2.5 points on the road at Ryan Field after coughing up a late lead to Wisconsin. Although Northwestern nearly shocked Indiana, my Penn State vs. Northwestern prediction and college football picks lean on the Nittany Lions' edge in the trenches. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. ET in Evanston, with the game airing on FOX. TOP PICK Who will win Penn State vs Northwestern: Penn State -2.5 I like Penn State up to -3 as a fade of last week's results. Penn State choked away a 10-point fourth-quarter lead in a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin, while Northwestern nearly upset reigning national champion Indiana on the road. That creates a natural let-down spot for the Wildcats, even if they are at home. More importantly, the Nittany Lions have a better net standard-down success rate and line yards differential, according to CollegeFootballData.com . Trench play and success rate on first and second downs are the two most predictive aspects in football handicapping , and both favor Penn State. Penn State vs Northwestern Over/Under pick: Under 46.5 The Under 46.5 is playable down to 45.5, with two slow-paced teams that like to pound the rock . Northwestern ranks 87th in offensive seconds per play , while Penn State is 104th, and both sit 34th in rushing rate against FBS opponents. Meanwhile, Wildcats QB Aidan Chiles has taken too many drive-killing sacks. Northwestern enters this one 113th in sack rate allowed and 127th in yards per rush against FBS opponents. Poor early-down rushing should put Chiles in long third-down situations, allowing Penn State to keep them from reaching the red zone. Penn State vs Northwestern combo I expect Penn State to punch first and control this game in the trenches , while Northwestern's weak rushing attack and sack problems should keep the scoring down. The Nittany Lions also own the standard-down advantage, which should help them stay ahead of the chains. I'm using Penn State's moneyline instead of its full-game spread to increase the win probability and protect against Northwestern's tendency to play its best football after halftime. Game: Penn State Nittany Lions (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten) @ Northwestern Wildcats (2-1, 0-1 Big Ten) History: 16-6, Penn State Last Meeting: 22-21, Northwestern (2025) Time: Friday, 8 p.m. (EST) Location: Ryan Field | Evanston, Ill. Radio: 99.5 FM | 103.7 FM | 1450 AM | SiriusXM 84, 257, XM App Odds: Penn State -2.5 | O/U: 45.5 Penn State vs. Northwestern Preview Injuries, Preview & Prediction This will be the 23rd meeting between Penn State and Northwestern. The Wildcats took a 22-21 win over the Nittany Lions in Beaver Stadium last season in what was James Franklin's final game at Penn State. The Nittany Lions are 7-3 all-time at Ryan Field, but Friday night will be the opening of the brand-new Ryan Field, an $870 million 35,000-seat stadium. Daryus Dixson Listed as Questionable Starting cornerback Daryus Dixson was listed as questionable on the initial and Wednesday availability reports. Dixson has started all four games and has allowed only three catches for 28 yards in coverage. Matt Campbell said Wednesday that Dixson was "dinged up" before halftime last week against Wisconsin, but he did practice on Wednesday. Not much has changed besides Dixson's status. Penn State is still waiting for Koby Howard and LaVar Arrington II to return from their injuries. Backup kicker Cristiano Rosa is a new addition to the availability report and is listed as out. Scouting the Wildcats On the other side of the availability report, Northwestern's starting tight end Luke Dehnicke has been downgraded from questionable to doubtful. He is the Wildcats' second-leading receiver with 11 catches for 208 yards. Northwestern also has starting corner Braden Turner and starting safety Damon Walters listed as questionable. Starting corner Josh Fussell is listed as doubtful. Northwestern took No. 5 Indiana to the brink on the road last Friday night. The Hoosiers escaped with a 29-23 victory. Wildcats transfer quarterback Aidan Chiles had perhaps his best game of the young season, passing for 293 yards and scoring three total touchdowns. His favorite target, however, was Dehnicke, who had seven catches for 140 yards. Northwestern's leading receiver, Griffin Wilde , had both receiving touchdowns. That's a big hit to Northwestern's passing attack if Dehnicke can't go. Last week against Wisconsin, Penn State struggled to cover Badgers tight end Jacob Harris , who had five catches for 105 yards, including the 72-yard score to seal the game. Dehnicke has played roughly half of his snaps from the slot this season and would likely be matched against one of Penn State's safeties, Jeremiah Cooper or Marcus Neal Jr. Neal really has struggled this year. He allowed both of Wisconsin's fourth-quarter touchdowns and has given up the most receptions and yards of anybody in Penn State's secondary. Northwestern has not done well establishing the run this year. The Wildcats rank 95th in the nation in rushing yards per game, and had only 32 yards and a touchdown by Chiles against Indiana. Photo Courtesy: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images On defense, the numbers are less impressive for Northwestern. The Wildcats' run defense has struggled, ranking 128th in the nation. The Hoosiers rushed for 271 yards and two touchdowns without leading rusher Turbo Richard for most of last week's game. Backup Lee Beebe Jr. had 24 carries for 203 yards and a score. Northwestern's pass defense isn't stellar either, ranking 80th in the country. This could be a big game for Penn State's receivers Brett Eskildsen , Chase Sowell and Zay Robinson . Sowell was the only wideout to record a catch in last week's loss. Eskildsen was able to break loose deep a few times, but Rocco Becht was off his game most of the night and missed multiple throws. While Northwestern's passing attack is very solid, it'll be difficult to throw against Penn State's No. 4-ranked pass defense, especially if Dixson is healthy. Running likely won't be much easier, but Penn State has struggled to contain scrambling quarterbacks like Chiles so far. This also could be a breakout game for Penn State's run game , and the same for the passing attack if the Wildcats are down three starting defensive backs. If Penn State's offense can get back on track against a weaker defense than Wisconsin's, then the first game at new Ryan Field will likely go to the visitors. Richard went down in the second quarter along the Indiana sideline as Northwestern’s Jamaal Johnson pulled him to the ground with a hip-drop tackle . Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti said Northwestern’s Brendan Flakes also hit Richard after he was out of bounds, but officials didn’t throw a flag. Trainers took Richard to the medical tent and then helped him to the locker room. He kept his weight off his right foot and didn’t return. “We’ll find out,” Cignetti said, per 247Sports . “You hate to see that happen to a good player, playing really well … He’ll do everything he can to get back.” Martin’s broken arm has kept him out all season. Indiana Hoosiers running back Turbo Richard is dealing with a suspected high ankle sprain from the No. 5 Hoosiers’ 29-23 win over Northwestern, and the injury leaves the defending national champions short on healthy ball carriers. Indiana was already playing without backup running back Khobie Martin, who has missed all four games with a broken arm. home.blurb: Penn State DB questionable for Northwestern game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Penn State DB questionable for Northwestern game After last week's news surrounding the injury status of Koby Howard , Penn State fans could be forgiven for not wanting to hear anymore bad news. Now though, a pivotal defensive starter could miss some time as well. Sophomore cornerback Daryus Dixson apparently struggled with an injury during the Wisconsin game and is currently listed as questionable for the game against Northwestern . For Dixson, this could be a minor setback for what has been looking like a breakout season for the young corner. He recorded his first interception of the season last week and played the most snaps out of anyone on the defensive side of the ball. Most impressively, he has only allowed three receptions all season long, with the longest only being 16 yards. Against Buffalo, he also recorded a blocked field goal, proving his versatility and importance to the squad. While Dixson should be good to go should he miss the Northwestern game, others are not as lucky. Defensive end Max Granville suffered a season-ending injury in the first game of the season, his second in as many years. As for Koby Howard , no one knows when he will likely return, but to expect him to only miss a couple of games would be wishful thinking. Penn State fans can only hope this Dixson injury is the last of its kind this season. The Crimson Tide moved to 4-0 with a devastatingly dominant 49-18 win against South Carolina . Sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell was flawless with 365 yards passing and four touchdowns. Mississippi State is in the midst of one of the great starts in program history, reaching consecutive 4-0 starts for the first time since World War II. The Bulldogs came from behind to stun No. 19 Missouri 31-24 behind 360 yards and three touchdowns from superstar quarterback Kamario Taylor . Alabama has dominated the matchup between these two teams all-time, holding an 86-18-3 advantage, including a 40-17 win in 2023. However, the last MSU win came in Nick Saban's first season -- can the Bulldogs turn the Tide? Alabama vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Super Kamario: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor has been the story of the early college football season. The Macon, Mississippi, native dreamed of playing in Starkville, and leads the SEC with 344.3 yards of offense per game. Taylor has thrown for at least three touchdowns in every start, including in road trips to Minnesota and South Carolina. With him in the lineup, suddenly anything seems possible at Mississippi State. Russell's rise: Taylor might be the best quarterback in the nation; he also might not be the best quarterback in this game. Since throwing a pair of interceptions in his first SEC start against Kentucky , Russell has been astonishing, throwing for 685 yards and seven touchdowns on 77% completion in wins over Florida State and South Carolina. Behind Russell's explosion, Alabama leads the nation in points per game against Power Four competition at 48.0 points per game. Best on worst: With so much attention on the quarterbacks, the secondaries will take center stage. Mississippi State has the worst passing defense in the SEC statistically, but the Bulldogs rank ahead of the Tide in both yards per attempt and passer rating allowed. Mississippi State has recorded nine sacks in four games, but getting a consistent pass rush could change the game. But like so many Alabama games before, the Tide will just find a way to pull away at the end in perhaps the best quarterback battle of the season. picks.headline: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know
picks.blurb: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS STATE SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS STARKVILLE — It's been nearly two decades since Mississippi State felt the joy of a win against Alabama. Sylvester Croom was roaming the sidelines as first-year coach Nick Saban and his Crimson Tide program were in the midst of a late season slide. Fast-forward 20 years and its Kalen DeBoer leading the way, looking to lead his team to 5-0 record for the first time in his tenure. On the flip side, Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby is looking to earn the first signature win of his young head coaching career while hosting No. 7 ranked Alabama for a nationally televised showdown on ABC. Here's everything you need to know to be prepared for what's a pivotal weekend for the Bulldogs program. Mississippi State Bulldogs running back Fluff Bothwell (24) and wide receiver Zion Ragins (7) react after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Game Information Game Information Mississippi State vs. Alabama Crimson Tide When : Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026 Kickoff Time : 11 a.m. CT Venue : Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, Mississippi TV Channel : ABC Radio : Bulldogs Sports Network Series Record : Alabama leads 86-18-3 Betting : Alabama (-5.5), O/u: 60.5 total points ( FanDuel ) DISCLAIMER : Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. What ESPN Thinks The brand of Alabama remains strong on the national radar and that's no different this week at ESPN with the Crimson Tide given a 74.2% chance of going into one of the most hostile atmospheres in all of college football and pulling out a win, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Mississippi State State continues its climb up the FPI rating system, coming in this week at No. 9 among SEC teams and No. 20 overall with key victories on the road at Minnesota and South Carolina plus another against then No. 19 Missouri. This starts one of the stiffest stretches for any team as the Bulldogs are set for a murderer's row-level slate with Alabama coming Saturday, proceeded by a BYE, on the road at LSU, home against Oklahoma and then another road trip to Austin to face the Texas Longhorns. The Bulldogs chances of winning out are slim at 0.1%, but do have a 97.5% chance of at least reaching bowl eligibility with six wins. When it comes to making the playoffs, Lebby's team has the sixth-best odds SEC teams at 23.8% to at least make the field, 1.6% to make the championship game and 0.5% chance to win the national championship. ESPN FPI (SEC) Rankings 1. Georgia 2. Texas 3. Alabama 4. LSU 5. Florida 6. Tennessee 7. Texas A&M 8. Ole Miss 9. Mississippi State 10. Oklahoma 11. Auburn 12. South Carolina 13. Missouri 14. Kentucky 15. Vanderbilt 16. Arkansas Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer walks off the field after a victory against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What DeBoer Is Saying What DeBoer Is Saying One of the hardest things for a coach to prepare his team for in a road game at Davis-Wade Stadium is the cadence of cowbells. Thousands of cowbells. "Personally, this is one of those stadiums that I haven't played in no matter where I've been," DeBoer said Monday. "What I hear from the people that I trust, is that it's going to be an absolutely crazy environment. We're going to be prepared for that. We talked about as a team this morning and we're looking forward to that challenge. "We know, this week, we've got to work on that crowd noise. There will probably be a lot of cowbells that we're hearing in practice in one form or fashion. Another thing is that it's just an early game. It's an 11 o'clock kickoff. We're a morning practice team and we've had some success in those morning games. We've got to go on the road and travel that morning. It's going to be a little different set-up that way too." The Bulldogs' defense has been very active this season at stopping explosive plays and keeping everything in front of them. They're disciplined, bring elite energy and effort with each down. "They play complementary football. They get the ball back, get off the field and get the ball back to the offense. I think it's timely stops. It's a group effort of guys flying around. They're going to be multiple in what they show you. "I have a lot of respect for them and what they are doing this time of the year. I think complementary football is what they're doing really well at Mississippi State. They're explosive. Obviously, that defense has to face that offense every day in practice. It's high level across the board." Mississippi State Bulldogs head coach Jeff Lebby looks on during the second quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Lebby Is Saying What Lebby Is Saying The Crimson Tide offense is full of big play athletes at nearly every position. Whether that's done with Keelon Russell's dual-threat combination, a four-headed backfield, Ryan Williams or any other weapon, Lebby knows his defense has to play assignment-driven, technically sound football to avoid allowing the game to get away from them early. "We're gonna have to do a great job tackling," Lebby said. "That's gonna be a huge piece of it. He's played really well. He's been incredibly productive. There's been explosive plays. He's got great talent around him. And so for us it's going to be about applying pressure, getting our fans really involved and excited about what's going on in between those white lines. "So for us it's kinda like I mentioned. We gotta get him off the spot and we've got to do a great job taking air out of it on the back end and making the plays when we get the chance." Alabama is tied for No. 24 nationally in sacks with 11 on the season. On the otherhand, Mississippi State has given up nine sacks on the season, which ranks No. 9 nationally, but the most alarming number was the four given up against Missouri in last week's 31-24 victory. And Lebby knows the biggest key to the Bulldogs upset bid will be keeping star quarterback Kamario Taylor upright to further establish himself as a Heisman Trophy contender. “[We] had moments where we were really clean, and had moments where we’ve got to continue to clean up,” Lebby said. “The fundamental pieces of it I’m gonna continue to talk about. Those guys playing clean fundamentally gives us the best chance to protect 1, but there were issues from a game standpoint. "We didn’t do a great job on the penetrator a couple times, and that’s part of being able to clean that up as we watch the tape, a huge focus for us this week.” Prediction : Mississippi State 42, Alabama 38 Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Former UCLA Coach Rick Neuheisel Predicts Winner of Alabama-Mississippi State Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS No. 7 Alabama (4-0, 2-0) travels to Davis Wade Stadium to face No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0, 2-0) in the SEC's lone ranked matchup of Week 5 (Noon EDT, ABC). These two programs are separated by an hour and a half's driving distance and are meeting for the first time in three seasons. Alabama and Mississippi State have been traditional staples on each other's schedules, although the 86-18-3 advantage held by the Crimson Tide makes for the most lopsided series in SEC history. The Bulldogs' last victory was in 2007, Nick Saban's first season in Tuscaloosa. The closest Mississippi State came within the last 16 meetings was in 2017; the game was tied in the final 30 seconds, and Jalen Hurts hit then-freshman wide receiver DeVonta Smith for a 26-yard touchdown pass to win it 31-24. The matchup features a pair of high-octane offenses Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) throws the ball during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Keelon Russell has been fantastic for Alabama, but the most impressive part of the offense is the run game. The Crimson Tide has been questionable in that department for the better part of three seasons, and it has very quickly found a combination of offensive linemen and running backs to correct the deficiency. On the other side, Kamario Taylor has lived up to the hype for Mississippi State. He guided the Bulldogs to a pair of road wins at Minnesota and South Carolina to bring excitement to a fan base desperate for optimism, and he delivered a 31-24 win over Missouri to a packed Davis Wade Stadium under the lights in Week 4. Neuheisel: "I see two matchups here that are really cool." CBS Sports' "Inside College Football" panel predicted the winner of the game between Alabama and Mississippi State on Tuesday. Former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel pointed to a pair of critical matchups between the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs while making his game pick. "Number one is the quarterbacks," Neuheisel said . "These two guys are both going to play on Sundays, both have just unique frames. They're 19 years old and they're just getting started." Despite the intrigue in the quarterback matchup, Neuheisel pointed to the other matchup as a deciding factor due to the current weather forecast for Saturday. "The second matchup is between the two defensive coordinators," Neuheisel said. "Both have been head coaches: Kane Wommack was at South Alabama, Zach Arnett was ironically right here at Mississippi State, these guys know how to play field position defense. It's supposed to rain a lot during the game, I think I've got to go, in that situation with Alabama." Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State (David Leong-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Thu, October 1, 2026 at 1:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide are coming off of a dominant Week 4 win over South Carolina, which represented their most complete performance all season. Now, Alabama is preparing for its most difficult test yet , as the Crimson Tide are heading on the road to battle the upstart Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday. Like Alabama, Mississippi State is 4-0, and the Bulldogs are also fresh off of a very impressive victory, having topped Missouri last weekend. Mississippi State boasts an explosive offense, and while its defense certainly isn't among the best, it has a pair of terrific cornerbacks in Kelley Jones and Jett Jefferson that could pose some problems for Keelon Russell and Co. So, are the Crimson Tide on upset alert heading into Week 5? ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score of the matchup using his SP+ metrics, and while he does have Alabama coming out on top, he thinks it will be a nail-biter, projecting a 32-27 win for the Tide in Starkville. A victory would absolutely comprise Alabama's most impressive of the campaign to date and would set Kalen DeBoer's squad up very nicely as it continues to proceed into the most challenging part of its schedule, which begins with the clash against the Bulldogs. While the Crimson Tide are undefeated, things haven't necessarily been easy for them thus far. Alabama took care of business without breaking a sweat against East Carolina in its season opener, but it trailed Kentucky 17-13 at halftime in Week 2 before dominating the second half. It also fell behind Florida State 21-6 in the first half the following week, but ultimately rallied for a 50-36 victory. The Crimson Tide definitely avoided a slow start versus South Carolina last Saturday, taking a 35-3 lead at one point in a 49-18 triumph. One thing is for sure: the version of Alabama that showed up in Weeks 2 and 3 absolutely cannot expect to waltz into Mississippi State and emerge with a victory. The Bulldogs are a significantly better team than either Kentucky or South Carolina, and the Crimson Tide fall behind early, they could be in some serious trouble. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is one of the top Heisman Trophy candidates at the moment, and the Bulldogs also possess a terrific backfield led by Fluff Bothwell. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has also been a fast riser, too. Alabama cannot mess around this weekend.

The Crimson Tide is now fourth in the nation in scoring at 48.0 points per game. Right behind them is Mississippi State at 43.0 ppg (15th). Despite all these numbers, Las Vegas is still a little suspicious of these two teams. FanDuel has opening odds of Alabama being a 4.5 point favorite over the Bulldogs with an Over/Under of 59.5 for a day game in Starkville. They are a split 2-2 against the Over/Under. Like most observers, the books figured on closer games against the Golden Gophers and the Gamecocks. But with the development of QB Kamario Taylor, the points have come much easier. Next, the Bulldogs face their first ranked team of the year. The Over/Unders for Bama thus far have not been big. Is it fair to say that the FSU game may have been a fluke or is that being too much of a Gump? It does not follow the trend of the Tide in their other three performances. Alabama has had a strong showing going over the Over/Under in all four affairs. Keelon Russell absolutely balled out on Saturday against South Carolina. If he can continue at that level of play against Mississippi State, there may be an exploding scoreboard in Starkville. The Bulldogs secondary is a bit on the sketchy side and the defense is prone to letdowns. For your consideration, this game will be played in Starkville with all those cowbells creating artificial noise. It will be much louder than Lexington was for the Crimson Tide in Week 2. The good side for Alabama is that they only have to travel about 90 minutes west to get to their destination. It's still six days away but the weather charts are calling for thunderstorms. Depending on how much wet stuff the field gets, there could be more dependencies on the running games by both teams. With an over/under of 59.5 and 4.5 point spread by FanDuel , the final score could look something like Bama 32-27. Are you buying that? I am expecting another big score. Thus, the Over/Under should go over. I also expect the Tide to cover the spread by at least -7. Give us your thoughts in Comments below.

away.blurb: Alabama football's initial SEC availability report is out ahead of the Mississippi State game. Right tackle Jayvin James is questionable after leaving Alabama 's home win against South Carolina. James was viewed as "very much questionable" after leaving with a lower-extremity injury late against South Carolina. Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said James is "working through it," and was on the practice field "a little bit." "It's what we expected, the progress he was making," DeBoer said. "Still questionable at this time." Defensive back Zavier Mincey is probable. Both linebackers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu were held out against South Carolina. DeBoer said both "will continue to miss some time," expecting Hill back before Umeozulu. Both are out along with Jorden Edmonds, Cayden Jones, Nick Sherman and Jeremiah Beaman. Left guard William Sanders left with an upper-body injury against South Carolina. DeBoer said he expects the Crimson Tide left guard to play against the Bulldogs. On his "Hey Coach" radio show, DeBoer said Sanders is "doing all right" and is practicing. Sanders did not appear on the injury report. But that's what Michigan is going to attempt to do this weekend after suffering a 20-19 loss to Iowa in Week 4. In reality, Michigan still holds its own fate in its hands . And that starts this weekend. The Wolverines hit the road for the first time and Michigan travels to take on Minnesota . The Gophers are coming off an impressive win over Washington, on the road, last weekend. Both programs enter Week 5 with a 3-1 record. Michigan is 78-25-3 all-time against Minnesota and this meeting will mark the 100th meeting for the Little Brown Jug. The Wolverines have won the last five games against Minnesota, but that doesn't mean Michigan can take this game for granted. Minnesota is a lot like Iowa. Neither program usually wows you on the offensive side of the ball, but defense and physicality can win them games. Minnesota hasn't quite lived up to expectations since P.J. Fleck was hired, but the Gophers haven't been an easy out when playing in Minnesota. Kyle Whittingham said this week that he feels like his team is 0-4, not 3-1. With a bye week coming up for Minnesota, this would be a great stepping stone to turning those feelings around and seeing Michigan play a complete game against a respectable opponent. Here's how our staff sees the game going. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Sometimes teams need wake-up calls and it's possible Michigan needed one. The Wolverines have been playing with their food way too often this season. Michigan has been the more talented team in every game, maybe the Oklahoma game being a toss-up, but the Wolverines have made errors in all of them. Assuming that carries over into this game, Michigan will get a needed win ahead of the bye week. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Michigan Football vs Minnesota - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Staff Predictions: Michigan Football vs Minnesota Von Lozon Fri, October 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines are on the road for the first time this season to take on the Minnesota Golden Gophers (noon on FOX). In this week's Roundtable, Maize n Brew staff members give their final thoughts on last week's loss to Iowa, some bold predictions for tomorrow's game and more! As we always do in these roundtables, give us some thoughts/takeaways from last week's game. I'm sure you have plenty this week! Von : Whatever discipline Kyle Whittingham once had, he surely didn't bring it with him from Salt Lake City to Ann Arbor. He must have left that at the Utah football facilities as their AD was forcing his ass out of there (allegedly!). Zach Libby : That play would only happen against Iowa. Grace : That's a tough one to lose because Michigan looked like it was starting to put a lot of stuff together. While I'm disappointed in the outcome, I'm still feeling mostly positive about the team overall. Andrew : I trust my colleagues to focus on the negatives — which they should after a loss — but allow me to sneak in some of the good. Bryce Underwood accounted for more than 300 total yards of offense and played his best game under his new offensive coordinator (to be clear, the interception was on the receiver). Not to mention, he did this against the best defense in the country and savant coordinator Phil Parker. There is no greater ceiling-raiser on this team than Underwood, and he is getting markedly better week over week. Scotty : My biggest takeaways from last week are that this team is a lot better than I thought, and these coaches are a lot worse than I thought. Kellen : I was watching the game at a friend's place as guests were arriving for a party. I was vacuuming the carpet when the kickoff return happened and I had a bad feeling at that point. After Michigan scored to make it 19-14, my friend said, "Okay, worst case scenario now is that they lose by one." This loss is your fault, Dyllon. I was upset with the penalties, but at least we had Qdoba and plenty of tequila shots to help numb the loss. Nick : I found myself really impressed with Michigan's offensive performance despite it only being 19 points. Iowa's defenses are always tough, but Bryce Underwood managed to put together his best game in a college uniform and the Wolverines had two receivers go for more than 100 yards. The lack of discipline though is really troublesome. If this game taught me anything, it's that the Wolverines have the chance to beat anyone on their schedule, but their lack of discipline won't allow that to happen. Charles : Michigan played its worst game of the season in a win over Western Michigan, and played its best game of the season in a loss to Iowa. That's just how football goes sometimes. The Wolverines have to be kicking themselves for completely blowing an opportunity to remain undefeated, but with every loss comes with a lesson. Now, Michigan has to learn from the loss and avoid a similar fate going forward. One loss is not the end of the world so as long as Michigan bounces back at Minnesota and keeps winning. If one loss turns into a losing skid, the season could become derailed. All in all, the Wolverines had a lot of positive takeaways from the loss to Iowa, so they need to channel those (improved pass attack, solid offensive line performance, run game showed some life, defense allowed just 13 points), while fixing the mistakes that cost them the game. What do you blame the most for the loss to Iowa: penalties, coaching, or something else? Von : This ultimately falls on the coaching staff. The Wolverines had the ball with just a couple minutes left in the game. Jason Beck should have dialed up a play to let Bryce Underwood throw the ball on 3rd-and-5 instead of handing it off to Savion Hiter and not picking up the first down. Even if the pass falls incomplete, I would have at least appreciated the killer instinct in trying to put the game on ice, while also giving your young quarterback some belief that the coaching staff trusts him and wants him to finish the game right there and then. It was a really bad way to end what was otherwise a great game called by Beck. Zach Libby : Giving up a kick return touchdown. Grace : My answer is something else. Honestly, it's tough when you've got Iowa making plays on the ball that the defense has tipped repeatedly. At first I put a lot of weight on the penalty on the final drive, but when it's all said and done, there were several things that fell just a teeny bit short throughout the game. That kept it close and Iowa was able to win the game. Andrew : I blame angering the football gods because this amalgamation of errors, miscues and tipped passes was clearly the universe righting the order of things after the Western Michigan game. If one error or bounce of the tipped ball goes the other way, Michigan beats Iowa. Blame does not fit in a nice, tidy box for this one — it is shared between the coaches and the players, and harkens back to their shortcomings in Week 1. Scotty : The penalties sucked, but I blame the coaching for that, so I'll say coaching here. I was very encouraged with the performance and I have a lot more confidence in this team than I did before the game. However, I think they're very poorly coached. Kellen : I think it comes down to penalties, but that's ultimately the fault of the coaching staff. As talented as this team is, they are not disciplined at all, and they ran into the opponent that is the best in the country at exploiting that. Hopefully this loss helped Michigan wake up and play smarter. Nick : I think it's a combination of both the coaching and penalties, since I see the penalties as a reflection of the coaching. The pre-snap penalties and late hits are so preventable, but unless there's real accountability for them, there won't be any sort of improvement in that category. Additionally, it seemed like the coaching and strategy in the game wasn't conducive to what was going on in the game, especially with the man coverage late in the game and the over-reliance on a run game that clearly wasn't working. It seemed as if Jason Beck and Jay Hill were over-reliant on the level of talent at their disposal and didn't think there was a chance for anything bad that could happen. Charles : The blame is certainly split between a number of things — giving up a kickoff return touchdown, a red zone interception, a failed fourth-down conversion in the red zone, an inability to ice the game away on the last possession, unnecessary penalties, and a questionable defensive play call on the last play. Kyle Whittingham said that if any of those moments went in the Wolverines' favor, they would have won, and he's right. It was somewhat of an unlucky loss, but sometimes you have to make your own luck, and Michigan failed to do so. It's hard to decipher which miscue deserves the most to blame, but I'll lean towards missed red zone opportunities and penalties. The Wolverines should have scored on at least one of those red zone trips, and the penalties have been an issue all season. Michigan simply has to be better in the fundamentals to take that next step, and doing the little things is what cost them against Iowa. Let's shift gears to the Golden Gophers. What worries you most about this Minnesota team? Von : The Gophers are a watered down version of Iowa. P.J. Fleck preaches taking care of the football, playing tough in the run game on both sides of the ball, and minimizing mistakes at all costs. They also pulled off a pretty big upset on the road last week against Washington, which came into the season with high expectations. I'm sure Minnesota has a bunch of confidence, while it's a completely different story for the Wolverines right now. Zach Libby : A blood soaked P.J. Fleck. Grace : They've managed to put some good games together. They held Washington to less than 100 yards rushing and will look to limit Michigan's run game. Michigan has struggled against the Gophers in the past. Andrew : Confidence. The Gophers are walking tall after a big win in Seattle and are ready to save their season. P.J. Fleck may be a little unhinged, but this team buys into everything he is selling. And you better believe he is reminding them of the 2024 game where Minnesota gave Michigan everything they could handle. Scotty : Drake Lindsey is off to a hot start this season. I love what I've seen from Michigan's defense this year and I feel good about the matchup, but Lindsey can play. Kellen : That win at Washington last week, with kickoff being at 11 p.m. EST, was super impressive. Granted, Washington is not the team that a lot of experts thought it would be, but doing that travel and winning on the road is incredibly admirable. P.J. Fleck has always slightly exceeded expectations at Minnesota, even if he put himself at risk to a parasitic infection with him wiping a player's blood on himself. It was equal parts epic and stupid, which made it a perfect encapsulation of why we all love college football. Nick : I don't know if there's anything about the team specifically that worries me, but it's a repeat of last week where I don't think Minnesota can come out and beat Michigan, rather Michigan will only lose the game if it beats itself. Going on the road for the first time only amplifies that, especially with the Golden Gophers kind of being a middle-of-the-pack team in the Big Ten. away.headline: Mounting injuries take a toll on Michigan offensive line
away.blurb: The Wolverines have started three different line combinations so far, and may have to go with a fourth this Saturday at Minnesota (12 p.m. ET, FOX) if tackle Blake Frazier — injured in the loss to Iowa — has to sit out. Those changes haven’t helped continuity, an important part of building a reliable offensive line, Harding admitted. Evan Link began the season at left guard, missed Week 2 due to injury and returned against UTEP as the starting left tackle, forcing Frazier to the right side to fill in for the sidelined Andrew Sprague. With Sprague’s status in limbo, and tackle Andrew Babalola ruled out since camp, Michigan has been shorthanded in recent weeks up front. When Frazier left the game last weekend against Iowa, a true freshman, Marky Walbridge, had to replace him. The good news — if there is some — is that there may be some light at the end of the tunnel. Harding is hopeful that Frazier may be able to suit up and play this Saturday, while Babalola is expected to be cleared to return next week. If he is, Babalola would have a full two weeks to reintegrate — Michigan is on a bye next week — before making his debut. ANN ARBOR, Mich. — While injuries and reshuffling have slowed the Michigan offensive line through four games, coach Jim Harding isn’t making excuses. The veteran o-line coach has seen it all and knows that a successful offense depends on the group up front, which he classified as a work in progress on Wednesday. “Truthfully, it’s not where I want it to be and where I think it can be,” Harding told reporters. “And that falls on me ultimately. You could say, ‘well, you’ve had this many injuries’ or ‘this many missed games,’ and frankly nobody cares. There’s injuries all across the country. We’ve got to do a better job.” “I think our pass protection so far has been really good, especially comparing the same players to last year,” Harding said. “I think we can be more consistent in the run game, getting more push.” Harding did see some good things against Iowa, who Michigan ran for 153 yards against, but explosive runs have been few and far between. Through four games, Michigan is averaging just 4.03 yards per carry and is one of nine FBS teams with one run of 20-plus yards or fewer. “The line of scrimmage was moving this past week, so that’s progress,” Harding said. “But it’s nowhere near where it needs to be in my opinion, or it should be. As frustrated as maybe some people are, there’s not anyone more frustrated (than me).” And then there’s the mystery with Sprague, who was suddenly scratched from the starting lineup the Friday before the UTEP game. If and when he returns, the Michigan would be six deep and in a much better spot. Daley, the All-American edge transfer from Utah, went down with an apparent lower-body injury on the penultimate play in U-M's 20-19 loss to Iowa. He was unable to get up as the Hawkeyes were rushing to the line of scrimmage to try and get off a final snap and the officials had to blow the whistle for an injury timeout. His diagnosis is unclear, but he is coming back from a notable injury after missing the end of the 2025 season and rehabbing all offseason from an Achilles. He has 16 tackles and a team-high three sacks through four weeks. For the second week in a row, his running mate, Nichols, is on the list. The junior edge was able to play against Iowa and his injury is also undisclosed. He's second on the team with 2½ sacks and is a key force on U-M's front. On offense, the most notable name is Marsh. The sophomore wideout has found his form the past two weeks, hauling in 17 total catches and more than 100 yards in each of those contests. He's made a number of highlight reel catches, including toe-taps along the sideline and one-handed snags. He's a fixture in Michigan's attack, having played 215 snaps and leading the team with 22 receptions. His name is also the biggest surprise, given he didn't show any obvious sign of injury last week, though he did at one point walk up the sideline and take off his helmet before momentarily sitting on a stationary bike. Sprague is the least surprising. He missed the past two weeks for unknown reasons and earlier this week Kyle Whittingham said the team was closer to learning the severity of his situation. away.blurb: We are going to find out a lot more about both of these schools with kickoff closing in. But ahead of the game, the official availability report came in. Offensive linemen Andrew Sprague and Manuel Beigel are officially out against Iowa. Which means, the Wolverines will assuredly keep the same lineup as they did last weekend. Evan Link will play at left tackle, while Blake Frazier slides over to right tackle. The other key to this injury report is that Beigel is out. He has been the Wolverines' starting Rhino this season, or sixth lineman. Without Beigel, we would expect to see Avery Gach as the Rhino against Iowa. For the Hawkeyes, the only player listed on their injury report is DB Kyler Gerardy, which means running back Kamari Moulton will play and be in the lineup. Moulton did not play last weekend against Northern Iowa, and he was listed as questionable earlier in the week. But the Hawkeyes are going to have their star from last weekend. Iowa enters the Big House with the top-ranked defense in the nation, but what do we really know about the Hawkeyes? If you were looking for reasons to be angry, Whittingham may have given you some ammo there. If you were looking for hope for the future, there is some hope there as well. Frazier was able to finish the game, which we’ll get to in a minute. The reason the injury was even scarier was because of the lack of reinforcements Michigan had behind Frazier. Link has performed admirably at left tackle, but could be a solution to some of the issues Michigan has on the interior if Babalola is able to play. With Sprague and Frazier both nursing injuries, Babalola provides depth if nothing else. The other big piece that was missing from the lineup was Michigan’s rhino, Manuel Beigel. Beigel missed Saturday’s game and gave way to Avery Gach. With good news came some concerning news. Blake Frazier was able to finish Saturday’s game, but is noted as day-to-day this week. home.blurb: With the Big Ten's new rules regarding injury reporting, much of the Huskies ' injury report was already known coming into Saturday. We also know that Minnesota will be down to their third-string center with starter Ashton Beers out and backup Brett Carroll out for the season. Washington remains out with a neck injury from spring practice. Washington should be approaching the re-evaluation point Jedd Fisch mentioned for him a few weeks ago, with a few scans scheduled to measure the progress of his neck, considering Fisch said that the third-year running back could be back as soon as October. Limar, like Moss, will be re-evaluated on November 1 after an elbow injury knocked him out of the final minutes of the Washington State game. The fourth-year running back had 12 carries for 50 yards and a touchdown before exiting with the injury. Carr suffered a hand injury during the Apple Cup and will be re-evaluated on November 1 with the other two, according to Fisch. He had 5 carries for 28 yards in his first career start before exiting. With Washington, Limar, and Carr out, Trey Cooley and Brian Bonner Jr. will combine to lead the backfield for the third straight week. Christian tore his Achilles during the spring practice the Huskies held at the Seahawks practice facility and is out for the season. CB Rahshawn Clark - GAME-TIME DECISION Clark popped up on the injury report this week with an undisclosed injury and has been listed as questionable all week. If he has to miss the game, Clark will be replaced by freshman Jeron Jones at nickel, unless Jones has to start on the outside for fourth-year corner Emmanuel Karnley. CB Emmanuel Karnley - GAME-TIME DECISION Karnley is questionable with a hamstring injury that he suffered against Utah State, which forced him to miss the Eastern Washington game. Fisch did say on Thursday that he is confident that one or both of Clark and Karnley should be able to play, but Elias Johnson would be in line to start on the outside if Karnley is out and Jones has to replace Clark in the nickel. The Washington Huskies have released their first game-day injury report of the season for the Big Ten opener against Minnesota. Hatchett returned to practice this week but seems like he is still a week away from returning from a wrist injury from last season. The Big Ten showdown brings a moment of tension for Ohio State, which suffered a 55-24 loss during its last visit to Kinnick Stadium in 2017. With one loss already, the Buckeyes can ill-afford a stumble as they enter a month that also includes trips to No. 6 Indiana and No. 18 USC . For Iowa, this represents a breakthrough opportunity on the heels of a last-second win at Michigan in Week 4. That victory propelled Iowa to 4-0 for the first time since 2021, when the Hawkeyes rose all the way to No. 2 in the AP poll on their way to an appearance in the Big Ten Championship Game. Beating the Buckeyes would put Iowa on a similar trajectory and send its playoff chances skyrocketing. Ohio State won the last two meetings by 28 (2024) and 44 (2022), but there are signs that these Hawkeyes are better equipped to stage a competitive battle as these Big Ten stalwarts square off in Iowa City for the first time in nearly a decade. Ohio State vs. Iowa: Need to know Iowa's offensive punch: Iowa ranks No. 48 nationally in total offense entering this showdown, which is hardly remarkable on the surface. But after ranking 117th or worse in total offense for the past five seasons, it's a marked improvement. The Hawkeyes struggled to run the football against Michigan last week, but quarterback Hank Brown led a game-winning drive capped by a touchdown pass to Reece Vander Zee on the game's final play. Considering the hostility of Michigan Stadium and the quality of the opponent, it was the sort of clutch, late-game execution that would have been unfathomable for the Iowa offense at any point over the past several years. Ohio State's defensive questions: Ohio State ranks just 27th in total defense through four games, down from finishing the 2025 season at No. 1 in that metric. Considering seven players from last season's defense were selected in the 2026 NFL Draft , it's not shocking that the Buckeyes have dropped off a bit. But the slide came with a cost in a Week 2 loss at Texas , when Ohio State's defense couldn't get off the field over the final 20 minutes as the Longhorns rallied from a 23-3 deficit to win 24-23. Illinois racked up 462 yards and 25 first downs on Ohio State last week. Though the Buckeyes won 42-19, it wasn't a banner day for coordinator Matt Patricia's defense, which comes into this game with some questions to answer. Jeremiah Smith making history: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is on a blistering pace with 33 receptions for 617 yards and seven touchdowns through four games. The junior star is one touchdown away from tying Chris Olave for most receiving touchdowns in program history and just five away from matching ex-Michigan star Braylon Edwards for most receiving touchdowns in Big Ten history at 39. Smith is on track to become the first player to ever lead the Big Ten in receiving yards three times. He's also likely to surpass K.J. Hill and Emeka Egbuka for most receptions in Ohio State history in the near future. However, the Hawkeyes aren't quite as stingy on defense as usual, which means slowing the Buckeyes down enough to keep the game within two touchdowns could be hard. Look for Iowa to make this a competitive game until Ohio State's superior skill talent (see: Jeremiah Smith) creates separation down the stretch. But it's close enough of a call that bettors seeing Ohio State -14.5 should consider the Iowa side. Happy prediction Friday, Hawkeye fans! Tomorrow is the day you've all been waiting for for some time - a colossal matchup at Kinnick Stadium between No. 14 Iowa and No. 5 Ohio State on Saturday (2:30 p.m. CT, CBS). After careful consideration, here's how I see this battle playing out. Where/When To Watch Matchup: No. 5 Ohio State (3-1, 1-0) @ No. 14 Iowa (4-0, 1-0) Scheduled game time: Oct. 3 at 2:30 p.m. CT Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Weather: 68 degrees Announcers: Brad Nessler (play-by-play), Charles Davis (analyst), Jenny Dell (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Cole Krueger) Before we talk about the actual football game, let's begin this pick by talking about the electric atmosphere we're about to witness inside Kinnick Stadium on Saturday. This is easily Iowa's biggest home game at least in five years (No. 3 Iowa vs. No. 4 Penn State in 2021), and you probably have to go all the way back to the 2006 showdown between the Hawkeyes and Buckeyes to find a more important game in Iowa City. Iowa fans have waited for this game since the schedule came out in February, and the buzz in this city is palpable right now. College GameDay returning for the first time in 20 years has only increased it. The crowd might be the only advantage Iowa has on the gridiron, though. Though it blew a 20-point fourth quarter lead at Texas a few weeks ago, Ohio State still might be the most-talented team in the nation. The Hawkeyes are going to have their hands full against the Buckeyes, but the one thing Iowa will always have? Heart. That competitive grit was evident in the thrilling comeback victory over Michigan last weekend, and the Hawkeyes will certainly need it to keep pace with an explosive Buckeye offense. Speaking of offense, how will Iowa stop Jeremiah Smith? Smith is not only the best wide receiver in the country, he may just be the best player in the entire sport. Not only is he fast and an excellent route runner, his 6-foot-4, 222-pound frame makes him a dangerous threat in 50/50, red zone situations. Smith is likely going to make a few big plays in this game, but what concerns me the most is Iowa trying to get pressure on Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin. The Hawkeyes are never going to be a blitz-first team under Phil Parker, but have you seen how accurate Sayin is? He's not much of a running threat, but Iowa has to get pressure on him if it wants to stay in this ballgame. I think the Hawkeyes will get to Sayin a few times, but I don't think it's going to be enough. Iowa is going to cover the spread and move the ball against a shaky Ohio State defensive front , but the Buckeyes just make a few more big plays to pull away for a victory. picks.headline: Greg McElroy Picks Florida-Missouri Winner in High-Stakes Week 5 SEC Showdown
picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks Florida-Missouri Winner in High-Stakes Week 5 SEC Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS College football analyst Greg McElroy has made his pick for No. 8 Florida at No. 25 Missouri. The ESPN host sees running back Jadan Baugh and the Gators' ground game as the biggest problem for a Tigers team that just lost its conference opener. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy picked Florida to win 31-24 on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. "Florida has a deeper offense," he said, "and Missouri's red zone issues, that's something that's difficult to overcome in this game." Florida jumped from No. 21 to No. 8 in the Top 25 poll after a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss. Missouri slid from No. 19 to No. 25 after it gave up the last 14 points in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. "So, for Missouri, this is got-to-have-it mode, given what's coming up here in the next few weeks," McElroy said. McElroy has liked this Florida team since the summer , when he said the Gators could play spoiler in the 2026 Playoff race. How can Missouri slow Jadan Baugh? Florida Gators running back Jadan Baugh (13) reacts after a play against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baugh, a junior from Atlanta, has 600 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns through four games. He ran for 142 yards and three scores against Ole Miss. That gave him five straight 100-yard games , a streak only Emmitt Smith and Fred Taylor had put together at Florida.
