That gave him five straight 100-yard games , a streak only Emmitt Smith and Fred Taylor had put together at Florida. McElroy called the Missouri run defense "Missouri's best unit against Florida's best player." The Tigers have stopped 45 runs at or behind the line of scrimmage, which he said ranks in the top six in the country. Quarterback Aaron Philo has completed 72% of his passes for 917 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Still, Florida throws only 26 times per game, which McElroy said ranks 103rd. "If Missouri can somehow hold Jadan Baugh under three yards a carry, then it goes squarely on Philo's shoulders, and we haven't seen it just yet," McElroy said. Florida's secondary faces Missouri passing attack Missouri Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons (13) passes the ball | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons has 11 touchdown passes and no interceptions, according to McElroy, and wide receiver Cayden Lee had 156 receiving yards at Mississippi State. Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons has 11 touchdown passes and no interceptions, according to McElroy, and wide receiver Cayden Lee had 156 receiving yards at Mississippi State. McElroy sees that as the biggest mismatch. He said Florida gives up about 250 passing yards per game and that Ole Miss threw for 298 against the Gators. "So, if Missouri is at, say, 300 passing yards, they have a real chance to potentially win the game," McElroy said. Florida may also get its top receiver back. Vernell Brown III leads the team with 17 catches for 271 yards , and Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said the knee injury Brown suffered against Ole Miss is a mild strain . Who wins Florida vs. Missouri? Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall talks with quarterback Aaron Philo (12) during a timeout against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy picked the Gators by seven. He noted Sumrall is 36-1 when his team makes more red zone trips than the other team, and he said Florida scores touchdowns on five of every six trips inside the 20. He noted Sumrall is 36-1 when his team makes more red zone trips than the other team, and he said Florida scores touchdowns on five of every six trips inside the 20. "I just think Florida has way too many ways to deliver the big haymaker and the knockout blow with how they run the football," McElroy said. No. 8 Florida visits No. 25 Missouri after beating No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28, and my Florida vs. Missouri predictions still lean toward the Gators being in a tricky road spot. The top pick is Under 57.5, while Missouri's first-half moneyline offers a way to account for the emotional win without fading Florida across 60 minutes. Head over to our latest college football picks for more Week 5 betting analysis. Who will win Florida vs Missouri: Florida -5.5 The Florida Gators just beat top-five Ole Miss 52-28, so a letdown argument is obvious with a road trip to face the Missouri Tigers ahead. But I'm not letting that erase the matchup. I'll play the Gators to -6. Florida ranks 14th in net adjusted EPA per play , while Missouri sits 72nd overall and 107th offensively. The Tigers' defense is the reason this is not a runaway. It ranks 31st overall and third in pass success rate allowed. Florida can attack the softer part of the matchup on the ground, where its rushing offense ranks fifth in EPA per rush against Missouri's 50th-ranked rush defense. There's not a ton here to get you believing in head coach Eli Drinkwitz either. Since 2024, Missouri is 1-9 versus ranked teams, with its only win coming against No. 24 Boston College in 2024. TOP PICK Florida vs Missouri Over/Under pick: Under 57.5 I'm playing the Under down to 57%. If there's any hangover from Florida, this is one of the best ways to capitalize on it. A few late stat-padding touchdowns from the Gators made this number overinflated. The Tigers rank sixth nationally in defensive success rate and third in pass success rate allowed. Florida will score, and I expect the Gators to cover, but they may need to earn points with longer drives instead of relying on constant explosiveness. On the other side, I anticipate the Gators' defense to make Missouri uncomfortable. That unit has allowed just 0.07 EPA per play on early downs. That should help keep Missouri behind schedule, especially given that its offensive success rate sits ranks in the triple digits nationally. Florida vs Missouri combo Missouri's defensive efficiency should keep this from becoming an early track meet, but Florida comes with the stronger profile in the downs that decide close games. The Gators convert 61.9% of third- and fourth-down opportunities , sitting sixth nationally, while Missouri's offense converts 42.9%, ranking 74th. That gives Florida a better chance to sustain the possessions that matter most after halftime, even if Missouri's field position and home environment produce an early lead. A competitive first half followed by Florida's superior talent and coaching taking over is the vision for this combo. First-year coach Jon Sumrall has brought one of the nation's most electrifying offenses to Gainesville, and he'll take that show to Missouri this week for another clash between ranked teams. UF is 4-0 (2-0 in SEC) for the first time since 2019 and has already matched its win total from Billy Napier's final season. They picked up their biggest win in years with an exhilarating 52-28 win over then-No. 6 Ole Miss behind 268 combined rushing yards and four touchdowns from Jadan Baugh and Duke Clark . Quarterback Aaron Philo ran one in too, tacking on a TD pass to give him seven on the year. Mizzou (3-1, 0-1) catches Florida 's fifth-ranked offense a week after falling 31-24 to the fourth-ranked offense in Mississippi State. Austin Simmons kept up as best he could with Kamario Taylor , throwing for 295 yards and three touchdowns, with Cayden Lee bringing in 11 catches for 156 yards and two of those scores. Jamal Roberts , starting at running back for the injured Ahmad Hardy , is third in the SEC with 395 rushing yards. Buy Florida vs. Missouri football tickets Here's when the Gators and Tigers square off this week. Florida football schedule: UF's next game What time is Florida vs Mizzou? The Gators and Tigers kick off at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, Missouri . Florida vs Missouri football prediction The Gators passed their first road test of the season two weeks ago at Auburn, a game they led by multiple scores for much of the second half. The two Tigers are tied for seventh in the SEC in allowing 20.8 points per game, but Mizzou is much better defending the run, surrendering just 100.3 yards per game, a hair ahead of Florida for sixth in the conference. They held Kansas , owners of the No. 49 run game in the nation, to just 80 yards on 36 carries, so don't be surprised if Jadan Baugh falls under his lofty averages. The question then becomes whether Aaron Philo can pace the offense, and nothing we've seen so far indicates he can't do it. Both offenses are likely to try to air it out against the other's weaker pass defenses (Missouri is 10th in the SEC in that category, Florida 15th). Eli Drinkwitz's side hasn't beaten a top-10 team in nine tries, though, with two of those coming in Columbia. UF should have enough offense to survive. By Braden Ramsey Published: Oct 1, 2026 · 3:10 PM EDT There are two ranked-on-ranked matchups in the SEC this weekend. Alabama-Mississippi State has the country's attention, but the Florida Gators ‘ trip to the Missouri Tigers can't be overlooked, even if the two programs have drastically different perceptions through four weeks. Entering play, Florida (4-0, 2-0 SEC) is everyone's darling. The Gators have scored 53.5 points per game and are up to No. 8 in the country. Meanwhile, Mizzou (3-1, 0-1 SEC) is clinging to a No. 25 ranking that folks believe it doesn't deserve . Greg McElroy thinks there's a recipe for the Tigers to pull an upset, but them toppling Florida. “For Missouri, this is ‘got to have it' mode,” McElroy said on his Always College Football podcast. “[But] I'm taking Florida to win the game, 31-24. Jon Sumrall is 36-1 when his team makes more red zone trips than the opponent… Missouri's red zone issues [are] difficult to overcome in this game.” McElroy believes Mizzou will have a shot to win if it can force the Gators to rely upon quarterback Aaron Philo instead of the rushing attack. “[Jadan] Baugh against Missouri's front, that's the heavyweight fight… Missouri's best unit against Florida's best player,” McElroy said. “The biggest mismatch might actually be Missouri's passing attack against Florida's questionable secondary that has yet to be tested, at least in… a throw-a-thon.” Florida has thrown the ball just 104 times this year, second-fewest in the SEC. Philo has been effective when passing, but has not had to shoulder the offensive load for the Gators yet. Until he does so, we won't know if he's capable or not. away.headline: Mizzou injury status for Ahmad Hardy, 2 starting DEs vs Florida on official SEC report
away.blurb: As expected, Mizzou (3-1, 0-1 SEC) will again be without star running back Ahmad Hardy , who opened the week on the Wednesday, Sept. 30, report as "out." The Tigers also listed starting defensive ends Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen as "questionable" for the game against the Gators , which Eli Drinkwitz indicated would be the case during his press conference Tuesday. A questionable designation means neither Smith nor Kitchen have officially been ruled out but will continue to be assessed throughout the week. If Smith can't play, Daeden Hopkins and Jaden Jones are Mizzou's likely starters at defensive end. Smith was helped off of the field during MU's win over Troy this past Saturday. He attempted to return after being evaluated for a lower-body injury in the second half but only lasted one snap before returning to the sideline. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of MU's Week 4 game against Mississippi State and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. Hardy's timeline for a return after being shot in the upper leg in May is still uncertain. Florida (4-0, 2-0) listed two wide receivers — Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton — on the report as questionable. Both players have been involved in the Gators' wideout rotation this year, and Brown leads the team in receiving. For the second straight week, Mizzou also ruled out right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. The Tigers added backup linebacker Bobby Washington as "questionable" to face Florida. DE Langden Kitchen (Questionable) LB Bobby Washington (Questionable) WR Vernell Brown III (Questionable) WR Bailey Stockton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. away.headline: Florida football injury update: VBIII, Bailey Stockton questionable for Mizzou
away.blurb: News Sports Autos Business Michigan Life + Home Entertainment Opinion Obituaries FOOTBALL Florida football injury update: VBIII, Bailey Stockton questionable for Mizzou Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Sept. 30, 2026, 8:53 p.m. ET Hear this story View Comments Florida football wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton have been listed as questionable for UF's game at No. 25 Missouri (October 3, 3:30 p.m., ABC) on the SEC's Initial Availability Report released on September 30. Brown III suffered a knee injury after an 11-yard run in the second quarter during UF's 52-28 win over Ole Miss and did not return. Stockton, meanwhile, suffered a back injury on a helmet-to-helmet targeting hit by Ole Miss safety Joenel Arguero, who was ejected on the play. He returned to field punts in the second half but has been limited in practice this week. If Stockton and Brown are both out, Florida could turn to receivers Eric Singleton Jr., Kahleil Jackson and Micah Mays Jr. for more snaps against Missouri. Singleton returned to the field after sitting out two-plus game with an ankle injury and caught a 38-yard pass against Ole Miss, while also forcing a pass interference penalty. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy, the SEC's leading rusher from 2025 with 1,649 yards, remains out while recovering from a gunshot wound in his leg. Also out for the Tigers (3-1, 0-1 SEC) are safety, JaDon Blair, running back Malae Fonoti, offensive lineman Josh Atkins and tight end Gavin Hoffman. Edge rushers Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith and linebacker Bobby Washington Jr. are questionable for Missouri. Brown leads the No. 8 Florida Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC) in receiving with 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 TDs. He's also been a weapon on special teams with two punt returns for TDs. Stockton, meanwhile, has 13 catches for 106 yards and 1 TD on the season. Florida football may need to turn to depth at WR "He played 8-9 snaps," said Florida football offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner, who coached Singleton at Georgia Tech. "He went deep three or four; he got a pass interference; he got the 38-yard gain. So, yeah, he brings a totally different element when it comes to being able to take the top off of defense than really anybody I've ever been around." UF has been relatively healthy so far under first-year coach Jon Sumrall, in part due to a strength and conditioning program under Rusty Whitt that focuses on building strength for injury prevention. Whitt is having players maintain a strict weight room schedule during the regular season. "We've put a lot of work in," Sumrall said. "You know, things that are strong are resilient and don't break easily. So there's a lot of work that's been put in by Rusty (Whitt) and Paul Silvestri and that group. Very grateful for our sports medicine team and strength staff, they all do a phenomenal job." Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun’s Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Follow him on X @KevinBrockwayG1.

away.headline: Final score, recap from Florida's Week 4 win vs Ole Miss in the Swamp
away.blurb: Florida ran out the clock after the interception and got the required first downs. Kati George spoke to Sumrall again after the game. Gators defense forces quick three-and-out — Florida 45, Ole Miss 28 (Q4 | 8:42) Ole Miss goes three-and-out without gaining a yard, burning just 29 seconds before punting it back to Florida with 8:42 remaining. Florida doesn't give Ole Miss much time to enjoy making it a three-point game. After London Montgomery's 74-yard kickoff return puts the Gators at the Ole Miss 26, Aaron Philo immediately finds Amir Jackson for 23 yards down to the 3. The Gators get an immediate spark on the ensuing kickoff, though, as London Montgomery breaks a 74-yard return to the Ole Miss 26. Florida plays conservatively after getting the ball back with 1:11 remaining. Jadan Baugh runs twice before Aaron Philo finds Dallas Wilson for four yards on third-and-11, bringing out the punt team. Alec Clark flips the field with a 70-yard punt that goes out of bounds at the Ole Miss 2. The Rebels pick up 29 yards on three plays but run out of time. Clark has only had three chances to impress as Florida's punter. This should put him on the map... somewhere. Florida keeps the Rebels out of the end zone from there. DJ Coleman violently breaks up a pass intended for Samari Reed on second down, and Chambliss can't connect with Horatio Fields on third-and-4. Florida starts buried at its own 13 after an ill-advised kickoff return but spends the next 7:15 methodically marching 87 yards on 15 plays. Jadan Baugh gets things moving with gains of seven and two before Aaron Philo converts third-and-1 with his legs. Baugh takes it from there. He gains three yards on a direct snap and punches it in from two yards out on the next play for his second touchdown of the game. The Gators lead by two touchdowns three minutes before the break. The Gators' defense figures it out after that, though. Frazier loses two yards, Jayden Woods drops Caleb Odom for a 5-yard loss and Florida keeps a third-and-17 completion to six yards. Lucas Carneiro connects from 36 yards out, cutting Florida's lead to 10-3 with 10:13 remaining in the half. Penalties wipe out Gators touchdown as drive unravels — Florida 10, Ole Miss 0 (Q2 | 12:34) Baugh takes over from there, gains two yards, then punches it in from four yards out for the touchdown. Jadan Baugh wasted little time getting Florida’s offense moving, ripping off a 12-yard run on the Gators’ first play from scrimmage. Aaron Philo followed with a quick out route to Luke Harpring for another first down, to move Florida into Ole Miss territory. Florida passed its first major test last weekend against Auburn, and while Jon Sumrall and Co. out-duked the Tigers, it was far from a perfect performance — particularly the penalty issue that has once again reared its head. The offense overall still looks potent and the defense, despite a few letdowns, appears to be rounding into form. Jadan Baugh led the way with 142 yards and three touchdowns

home.headline: Missouri’s Ahmad Hardy gets unfortunate injury timeline from scary gun shot incident
home.blurb: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy’s return remains several weeks away after the consensus All-American suffered a gunshot wound to his upper leg in May. The Tigers had already listed the running back as out for Saturday’s road game against Mississippi State. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz said back in August that Hardy would need a multi-week ramp-up period once he was cleared to resume practicing. With Hardy still unable to practice, his return to game action still remains weeks away. ESPN college football senior writer Pete Thamel provided the latest update on Saturday during College GameDay. “Ahmad Hardy’s comeback for Missouri keeps hitting bumps,” said Thamel. “He still has not practiced.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Hardy required emergency surgery after being shot at a concert in Mississippi . His continued absence comes after a standout 2025 campaign in which he led the SEC with 1,649 rushing yards and scored 16 touchdowns. He also rushed for 300 yards and three touchdowns versus the Bulldogs last season. The Tigers travel to face a Mississippi State team that entered Saturday ranked No. 24 with a 3-0 record, its first appearance in the rankings since 2022. The Bulldogs finished 5-8 last season and 2-10 in 2024, while Missouri defeated Mississippi State by a combined 88-47 across those two meetings. The Tigers opened the season with a 54-14 win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff before defeating Kansas in Lawrence and beating Troy in Week 3. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. Smith and Kitchen were Mizzou's starting defensive ends in each of their first three games of the season, but over the past two game weeks, both players have left the field with injuries and were unable to return. Smith was helped off the field during the first half of Mizzou's Week 3 win over Troy due to an ankle injury. He attempted to return in the second half but only remained on the field for one play. The fifth-year senior did not play in MU's loss at Mississippi State this past Saturday. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of the game against the Bulldogs and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. "Both are doing the very best they can to get back," Drinkwitz said. "I doubt they can participate in much of any practice today (Tuesday), but both of those guys are experienced. You know, our protocol is you have to practice by Thursday in order to be available for the game. Life in the SEC, that's kind of how we go about it with guys who are questionable." picks.blurb: Staff predictions for Virginia vs Florida State — a high-end rematch on deck Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB To keep pace and maintain a tie for first place in the ACC, Virginia must conquer Florida State in its first true road game of 2026. An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. This should be a Cavaliers win by multiple scores. Steve DeShazo: Virginia 31, Florida State 27 Saturday brings Virginia's first true road game of 2026. It comes against a proud and talented team that has not played up to its capabilities and may be competing to save Coach Mike Norvell's job in the same way I believe the Cavaliers did for Elliott last year. FSU's offensive skill trio of quarterback Ashton Daniels, receiver Ousman Kromah and receiver Duce Robinson will be a handful for the Cavaliers to contain. Beau Pribula could have a field day passing against the Seminoles, and it may be mandatory to keep Virginia close. The Cavaliers have yet to win a close game or pull out a victory away from home this season. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images FrankDNole Fri, October 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Florida State hosts the Virginia Cavaliers for the first time since 2014, a 34-20 Seminole win, on Saturday at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m., and the game will be televised on ESPN2. Of the 21 meetings between FSU and UVA, Saturday marks only the third time (2006, 2010, 2026) that neither team is ranked in the Associated Press Top 25. Florida State (2-2, 0-1 ACC) and the Cavaliers (3-1, 1-0 ACC) will meet for the second straight season and the 21st time overall in UVA's first true road game of the '26 season. FSU and UVA have not met in back-to-back seasons since the 2010 and 2011 seasons, with FSU holding a 15-5 all-time record against UVA, including a 9-1 record at Doak. Virginia's only victory came in 2011 when the Wahoos defeated the then-No. 23 Seminoles, 14-13. UVA will be trying for its third consecutive win and fourth in its last five meetings with the Noles. Saturday will be a rematch of last year's double-overtime loss by then-No. 8 FSU in Charlottesville, which ended with a game-sealing interception in the end zone by the Cavaliers. The victory was UVA's first over a top-10 opponent at home since defeating then-No. 4 Florida State 26-21 in 2005. CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Fans of the Virginia Cavaliers rush the field to celebrate after a game against the Florida State Seminoles at Scott Stadium on September 26, 2025 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Ryan M. Kelly/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia's defense comes into the contest allowing just 130 passing yards per game, the fifth-fewest in the nation and the lowest in the ACC, and ranked 14th in total defense, giving up just 247 yards per game. Opposing quarterbacks sport an 84.2 efficiency rating, the lowest in the country. UVA is one of 20 FBS teams allowing fewer than 14 points per game. The Cavaliers have held two of its four opponents without a touchdown and only allowed a total of 52 points on the season. On offense, UVA quarterback Beau Pribula ranks fifth nationally in passing efficiency (194.1), with 11 touchdown passes, tying for seventh in the country, and tied for fourth in the ACC. Eighteen Cavaliers have caught a pass this season, and each of UVA's last three games has featured double-digit pass catchers. Pribula has completed 66 of 86 passes and ranks fourth in the nation with a 77% completion percentage. The Seminoles are coming off their second win of the season after unimpressively beating outmanned Central Arkansas, 34-7. The Noles went 4-for-4 in the Red Zone against Central Arkansas and are now 17-for-17 to begin the 2026 season. FSU's 17 Red Zone conversions are the 4th most in the country among the 19 teams that are still perfect inside the 20. FSU QB Ashton Daniels is 58-of-97 passing for 928 yards and six touchdowns, with 142 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns. He has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all four games. Daniels is the only player in FBS in 2026 with multiple rushing and passing touchdowns and a two-point conversion. On the season, the Noles' offense is ranked a not-so-nice 69th in total offense, 76th in the nation in 3rd down conversions with just a 40.8% rate on 20-of-49 attempts, and tied for 63rd in scoring offense with a 32-point average per game. FSU's 126th-ranked total defense is allowing 430 total yards per game, 290 passing yards per game (135th out of 138 FBS teams), and ranked 121st in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 46% of the time on third-down attempts. Florida State is trending as a 2.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 51.5 points according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday's showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we've posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Curt Weiler (season record: 4-0, 2-2 ATS) Considering FSU's defensive problems against talented teams this season, it's hard to predict the success will begin against a Virginia offense, which has thrown 15 touchdowns to one interception this season while rushing for nearly 200 yards per game. And that doesn't even factor in a Virginia defense which is second in the ACC in yards per play allowed (4.1) on a team that has a plus-five turnover differential this season. FSU will need its home-field advantage to work overtime to make up for what feels like a talent discrepancy, as wild as that is to say considering Virginia has won at Doak Campbell Stadium exactly one time. Virginia 31, Florida State 24 Matt Minnick (season record: 4-0, 3-1 ATS) This game is FSU's season. A win on Saturday and the 'Noles move to 1-1 in ACC play and a chance to really establish some momentum the following week with a suddenly vulnerable Louisville squad. Lose to UVA, and it becomes hard to see Florida State avoiding a tailspin that results in a 3-9 type season. When you look at the advanced stats, Florida State's offense is respectable in many areas. It's still a small sample size, but adjusted for SOS, the 'Noles have the 18th best offense overall according to FEI, better than Nebraska, Texas, UCLA, LSU, SMU, Louisville, Virginia Tech, UVA, and a host of other teams with better records. Buoying the FSU offense are their explosive plays, ranking 36th in points per drive and 38th in yards per play. However, there is one area FSU's offense really struggles in, and that is "busted drive rate" where the 'Noles rank 90th. A "busted drive" is defined as a drive that gains 0 or fewer net yards, and here in lies Florida State's biggest problem. FSU's boom and bust offense does a nice job of putting points on the board in bunches, but when you have a defense that cannot get off the field (even when playing inferior opponents), it is essential that you consistently sustain success on offense. Otherwise, every busted drive results in your opponent receiving better and better field position and chewing up more and more of the clock. Not playing complementary football has been a theme under Norvell, and thus far this season is no exception. Virginia's defense admittedly has not faced a murderer's row, but they rank 13th in defensive busted drive rate. If the busted drive trends for both teams hold, it's hard to see Florida State emerging victorious. But if FSU can find a way to limit their three and outs and turnovers, the Seminoles might be able to hit enough explosives to outscore the 'Hoos at home. For the second time this season, FSU finds itself a short underdog at home, a typical "sharp spot" for betters in Vegas. Similar to the SMU game, I think FSU has its chances but just can't quite find a way to get the W. UVA 35, FSU 34 Jordan Silversmith (season record: 4-0) Last year's loss to Virginia turned Florida State's season sideways at a pivotal moment. Saturday will do the same thing. UVA is favored by Vegas — on the road — because they are the better team. The Cavs are the most experienced squad in the country and have an identity on both sides of the ball. Meanwhile, Florida State is still finding itself. On offense, they are boom-or-bust, producing explosive plays on the ground and through the air but unable to sustain drives. Defensively, FSU's defensive coordinator Tony White apologized to the offense after the Central Arkansas game for letting the Bears hold the ball for 40 minutes of time of possession. That says all that anyone needs to know about where the Seminoles are on that side of the ball. Even if FSU technically has better players, as Virginia is ranked 57th in 247Sports' Talent Composite, UVA has the better, coach, quarterback, and knows how to win. Virginia wins and covers. UVA 31, FSU 27 NoleThruandThru (season record: 4-0) I'm just here so I don't get fined. FSU 31, Virginia 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 3-0) All week I've been setting up how this is a bad match-up for FSU and how the more experienced, better coach, better quarterback, and better match-up UVA team should win, so naturally I'm going with the 'Noles. Boom or bust offenses work better at home than on the road, and this is UVA's first true road test of the year, as their only game away from the comforts of Charlottesville so far was a neutral-site loss to West Virginia. FSU 28, UVA 27 Jon Marchant (season record: 2-0 ) Virginia's Beau Pribula is very good at keeping Virginia ahead of the chains, whether it's with quick passes or his legs. However, if you can get Virginia into obvious passing downs, that's where he struggles. Unfortunately for FSU, the Noles' defense is terrible on passing downs, so I don't think it's a good matchup for FSU as far as that side of the ball goes. Meanwhile, the Seminoles' offense is very boom or bust—if they hit an explosive play, they have a chance to score. It's inherently an inconsistent way to play offense and means you will get a wide range of results from game to game. Does FSU have a chance in this game? Yes; it depends on 1) whether the defense can get even one or two stops and 2) how many explosive plays the offense can connect on. It's just not very likely. Virginia 34, FSU 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 4-0) I think we could see a similar game to last year's loss by Florida State. A shootout at times with Virginia pulling away. UVA 38, FSU 27 Tony Morris (season record: 2-0) It is time to right the ship (hopefully). Sit back and watch this Ous and Wisner masterclass of 200+ rushing yards. This simply comes down to if the defense can get the stops (even if it's just a couple). FSU's offense will do its part. Noles 31, Cavs 24 Frank DaNole (season record: 2-2) This will be the game when everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are only 2.5-point underdogs for a reason. Vegas knows it, and the Seminoles know it. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed last year when Alabama came to Tallahassee. The Seminoles may not dominate at all three positional units for the entire game, but in the end FSU will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their more talented, deeper, and better coached UVA opponents. Noles247.com staff predictions for Florida State's game versus Virginia at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Fla. on Saturday afternoon: Virginia's defense is a solid, though far from outstanding, unit. But in a game where possessions are going to be limited, I question Florida State's ability to slow down the Cavaliers' offense enough for Ashton Daniels and company to keep up with them, given what they've shown over the first month of the season. That starts in the trenches, where Virginia appears to have a significant advantage over the Seminoles' undersized defensive line. Even if Florida State can come out firing as they did early against Alabama , the Cavaliers will stick to what has brought them success this season and wear down the Seminoles' front as the game rolls into the second half – where they could be hurt by play action from Pribula as the second level gets antsy trying to jump into the backfield. The path to victory for Florida State comes from putting Pribula under the pressure he hasn't faced this season, forcing him into a mistake, and capitalizing with points off a turnover. But between Pribula and Daniels, the latter has been more prone to do so, and when the possession battle will be so important, one of those unforced errors could be costly for the Seminoles' chances of coming away with the victory. I think Florida State's offense will find some success, especially from Ousmane Kromah and the rushing attack. But as the game continues, the Seminoles' defense will struggle to get off the field, and Virginia will control things on the ground on its way to a win in Tallahassee. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 20 I find this to be a particularly interesting matchup as both have multiple ways to win. There a lot of "good vs. bad" matchups for both teams in this game. Virginia's ability to run the ball vs. FSU's 1200 thread count soft run defense. Florida State's skill talent on offense vs. a decidedly mediocre Cavalier secondary. Etc. Etc. The position that I will be the deciding factor is quarterback. Both teams will score, and Virginia will 100% limit the overall possessions by holding onto the ball. That means the importance of every possession is magnified. Every explosive you hit carries that much more weight, but every turnover is catastrophic. It all comes down to which team plays a cleaner game and limits unforced errors. I'm taking Virginia. Prediction: Virginia 34, Florida State 27 Florida State can win this game, but I am not convinced they will. My concerns is that Virginia , led by quarterback Beau Pribula , will find consistent success running into the heart of the FSU defensive line, controlling the game, the clock, and exhausting a defense that lacks capable depth and talent. An offense with the oldest offensive line in the country can control this game and should be able to manufacture multiple clock-eating touchdown drives against a Seminole defense that leaves plenty to be desired. They are efficient through the air, though they aren't built to push it down the field aggressively. My reason for optimism when it comes to the Seminoles is that I find Virginia's defense to be susceptible. In the loss to West Virginia , the Cavaliers struggled with a quarterback who ran at them in key moments, though Michael Hawkins Jr. has more wiggle than Ashton Daniels . A couple physical backs for the Mountaineers found success, too, and I think Ousmane Kromah , who should probably see his heaviest workload of the season, can do the same. Also, Virginia will give opportunities on the outside in 1-on-1 coverage and FSU can win there, specifically Duce Robinson who will likely be very motivated after his performance, which included some tough moments, in Charlottesville last season against UVA. Finally, UVA safety Ethan Minter is a player that can be attacked on the seam or vertically with athletic wide receivers. Game can easily swing via turnovers, and that is an area where Virginia is far better than FSU at not committing them on offense and forcing them on defense. I don't have strong feelings either way with one team being an overwhelming favorite. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 28 I've gone back and forth on this game. To be honest both teams are mediocre middle to bottom half of the ACC caliber teams right now. Both quarterbacks leave a lot to be desired. The skill on defense is not up to snuff with years past for either program. That being said, UVA does possess the better offensive line while FSU has the superior skill talent. What does all of that mean? Well it's going to be a battle of styles. Florida States passing attack against UVAs rushing attack. FSU must find explosive wins in the passing game at a more consistent rate while UVA tries to control the ball with a high success rate rushing attack. If Ashton Daniels can be aggressive against the man looks UVA will show him then FSU can win this game. If Ashton Daniels is passive this is going to get ugly in a hurry. I'm going to try a bit of optimism… Prediction: Florida State 34, Virginia 27 Kolby Crawford Everything is telling me to pick Virginia. Bad roster construction up front on both sides, an undersized line that can't hold up against a team built to run right at you, a season already bleeding attendance and goodwill. Which is exactly why I think Norvell comes out with a great plan and jumps on them early at home. Call it surprise, call it vibes, whatever it is, I feel it this week. I still believe this season takes a downturn fast from here, but this is one of the last wins they scrape out before it does. Slang that thing, Ashton. Prediction: Florida State 27, Virginia 23 Virginia had a promising start to the season but that loss to WVU in pretty convincing style is starting to negatively shape my perception of this team. To me the eyes test doesn't bear out against the advanced analytics. F+ has them as a top 25 defense and not a top 25 offense. That doesn't really track with what I see. Their offense is plodding and efficient. They use their mobile QB well, get their 3-4 yards a pop with a well structured IZ scheme, and then work for shots over the top off of play action. Think our offense from last year but without Duce and maybe a more consistent QB. Their defense struggled against WVU. To be honest, they looked good against NCSU but my middle school flag football team could look good against a Dave Doeren offense. Their secondary seems a bit slow and I think if you can spring into the second level you can rip off some chunks. away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. The second half was a complete 180, as Kentucky shut out South Alabama and pulled away for a 45-21 victory, and the victory improved Kentucky to 3-1 overall and 1-1 in SEC play. Now, the Wildcats will take on a struggling South Carolina team on the road. The last time Kentucky was on the road, the Wildcats defeated then-No. 9 Texas A&M, 31-21, in College Station. The victory showed how strong Kentucky's defense can be while also giving quarterback Kenny Minchey an opportunity to show what he can become as he continues to develop under first-year head coach Will Stein. South Carolina Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2) The Shane Beamer era is facing increased pressure in Columbia, as South Carolina enters the matchup on a seven-game SEC losing streak. The Gamecocks' last SEC victory came against Kentucky on Sept. 27, 2025, when South Carolina defeated the Wildcats 35-13. South Carolina opened the 2026 season with a dominant 57-0 victory over Kent State, but the Gamecocks have since struggled against SEC competition. South Carolina lost 41-34 at home to Mississippi State before falling to Alabama 49-18 on the road this past weekend. The loss to Alabama dropped the Gamecocks to 0-2 in SEC play. Now, Kentucky comes to Columbia, making this a potentially significant game for Beamer and the Gamecocks. Kentucky is also looking to snap a four-game losing streak against South Carolina. Doing so under Stein would give the Wildcats another significant road victory during his first season. South Carolina will also be without star EDGE Dylan Stewart, who has been suspended indefinitely by Beamer and more than likely will not play against Kentucky. Stewart's suspension came after the Gamecocks' loss to Alabama, during which he threw a punch at Alabama tight end Josh Ford and had a heated interaction with South Carolina's coaching staff. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains one of South Carolina's biggest offensive weapons. The dual-threat quarterback opened the season with 270 passing yards and three touchdowns in the Gamecocks' win over Kent State. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is another player Kentucky will need to account for. Harbor returned to South Carolina for the 2026 season alongside Sellers and remains one of the team's most important receiving threats. Junior running back Matt Fuller is also a name to watch in the South Carolina backfield after showing his ability as both a runner and receiver. Game: Kentucky Football vs. South Carolina Gamecocks Location: Williams-Brice Stadium — Columbia, South Carolina Date: Saturday, Oct. 3 Time: 4:15 p.m. ET TV Channel Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: Kentucky opens as a 2.5-point underdog, according to FanDuel . ESPN gives Kentucky a 42.1% chance of winning. My Early Prediction: Kentucky has already proven it can win on the road after defeating then-No. 9 Texas A&M. Why can't the Wildcats do it again? South Carolina is on a seven-game SEC losing streak and will be without Stewart, while Kentucky enters the matchup ranked No. 24 in the AP Top 25 and coming off a dominant second half against South Alabama. Kentucky also has plenty of motivation to snap its four-game losing streak against the Gamecocks. Why not us? Final Score: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 27.

While the hype and excitement are there, the Wildcats have a big-time game on Saturday on the road against the South Carolina Gamecocks. picks.headline: How No. 24 Kentucky football & South Carolina match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 19 of 25 passes for 177 yards with one touchdown throw in UK’s 45-21 victory over South Alabama last week. For the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey, a fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, is completing 68.3% of his throws for 876 yards. The Notre Dame transfer has thrown eight TD tosses vs. one interception. • South Carolina’s LaNorris Sellers is 2-0 as a starter vs. Kentucky. In those two games, Sellers has completed a combined 21 of 28 passes for 319 yards with two TD throws vs. one interception and has also run for 70 net yards on 22 carries. On the season, Sellers, a 6-3, 238-pound fourth-year player, has completed 62.1% of his throws for 833 yards with six TDs but has thrown four picks. A Florence, South Carolina, product, Sellers has run for a net 244 yards and a touchdown. Advantage : South Carolina Running backs • Kentucky is coming off the first game in school history in which the Wildcats had three running backs rush for 100 yards or more in the win over South Alabama. CJ Baxter 6-1, 230-pound, fourth-year player who transferred from Texas, led the way with 149 rushing yards and a touchdown vs. USA. Junior Jason Patterson went for 137 yards and three touchdowns against the Jaguars, while Oklahoma transfer Jovantae Barnes ran for 100 yards and a score. On the season, Patterson is sixth in the SEC in rushing (326 yards) and Baxter is eighth (313). A 5-10, 204-pound third-year player, Patterson is leading the SEC in yards per carry at 8.15 yards a rush. • South Carolina’s Matt Fuller leads the Gamecocks in rushing with 384 yards (fourth in the SEC) and in receptions with 13 (for 113 yards and a touchdown). In South Carolina’s 35-13 win over Kentucky last season, Fuller, a 5-11, 221-pound third-year player from Jesup, Georgia, ran for 48 yards on 19 carries. Jabree Coleman has run for 147 yards this season but is averaging 8.6 yards a carry and has scored three touchdowns. Isaiah Augustave has run for 107 yards in 2026 but is averaging 8.2 yards a carry and has scored two TDs. Advantage : Kentucky Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby has 13 receptions and leads the Wildcats in receiving yards with 226. LSU transfer Nic Anderson caught two passes for 21 yards vs. South Alabama. Southern Utah transfer Shane Carr caught his first UK touchdown last week against USA and finished with two catches for 22 yards. • South Carolina’s Nyck Harbor ranked No. 1 on The Athletic’s 2026 college football “Freak’s List.” A 6-5, 239-pound product of Washington, D.C., Harbor has an 82.5-inch wingspan and has run a 10.1-second 100-yard dash. On the football field, Harbor has 11 catches for 169 yards and a touchdown in 2026. In last season’s win over UK, Harbor caught one pass for 10 yards. Mazeo Bennett Jr . has 10 catches for 169 yards and a TD this season. In South Carolina’s 31-6 victory over Kentucky at Kroger Field in 2024, Bennett caught three passes for 63 yards and a touchdown. • Kentucky’s Henry Boyer tied for the team lead with three catches in the win over South Alabama. A 6-6, 270-pound senior from Chicago, Boyer has made seven catches for 110 yards and two TDs on the season. Ex-Covington Catholic star Willie Rodriguez leads the Wildcats in receptions (17) and is second in receiving yards (137). Second-year player Mikkel Skinner has seven catches for 91 yards and a TD. • South Carolina’s Brady Hunt has made nine catches for 81 yards and has a long reception of 20 yards. Hunt caught one pass for 15 yards vs. UK last season. Maurice Brown II has five receptions for 38 yards and a touchdown. Brown caught one pass for 10 yards against Kentucky in 2025. Offensive line • Through four games, Kentucky center Coleton Price is drawing rave reviews from Will Stein. Of the 6-3, 308-pound Baylor transfer, Stein said “He’s one of the best players on our team. I think he’s one of the best players in the country, specifically at his position. And he’s a leader. He’s a smooth athlete. He’s powerful. So I would say he’s playing very well.” • A highly-regarded transfer from North Carolina State, South Carolina left tackle Jacarrius Peak missed the first two games of 2026 as he recuperated from an offseason knee injury. However, Peak has now returned to claim a starting position. True freshman right tackle Darius Gray was the No. 2 interior offensive line prospect in the high school class of 2026 and has started all four games for far for the Gamecocks. Gray started at left tackle the first three weeks but flipped to right tackle for last week’s 49-18 loss at Alabama. Advantage : Even Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace leads the Wildcats in sacks (2.5) and tackles for loss (three). The 6-4, 291-pound Cincinnati product is also tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (three) and has both an interception and a pass breakup. • South Carolina star end Dylan Stewart was suspended by Gamecocks coach Shane Beamer after Stewart drew a penalty for punching an Alabama player during last week’s blowout loss to the Crimson Tide. In two previous games vs. Kentucky, Stewart had a combined seven tackles, 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. Right defensive tackle Tomiwa Durojaiye has made 10 tackles and recorded two sacks. The 6-4, 291-pound Durojaiye started his college career at UK in 2022 and has subsequently played for West Virginia, Florida State, Illinois and now South Carolina. • After Kentucky weakside linebacker Bo Barnes was ejected vs. South Alabama for targeting, fifth-year player Alex Afari logged his most significant playing time of 2026 and led the Wildcats in tackles with nine. Because of uncertainty about his eligibility, Afari did not have a full preseason in the new UK defensive system. “I think he’s becoming more instinctual in this defense. (It) takes some time to get used to, just because it’s a different scheme than he was used to,” said Kentucky coach Will Stein. “When you know what to do, you can play more aggressive and make more plays.” • South Carolina MLB Fred “JayR” Johnson , a 6-3, 241-pound third-year player, led the Gamecocks with eight tackles in the loss at Alabama. WLB Justin Okoronkwo is South Carolina’s leading tackler on the season with 26. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior free safety Jordan Castell is the second-leading tackler in the SEC with 36 stops. A transfer from Florida, Castell also has two interceptions and two passes defended. Strong safety Ty Bryant is 11th in the SEC in tackles with 30. • South Carolina nickelback Quay’sheed Scott was the starter at the same position last season for Kentucky. A 5-11, 208-pound product of Marion, South Carolina, Scott has made five tackles and successfully defended three passes in 2026. Strong safety Peyton Williams is third on the Gamecocks with 16 tackles and has an interception. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 4 of 5 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 52 yards. Punter Thomas O’Hara , a transfer from Murray State, is averaging 40.7 yards a kick on 11 punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Punt returner Brock Coffman lost a fumble that set up a South Alabama touchdown last week. • South Carolina punt returner Vicari Swain ran two punts back for touchdowns (45 and 58 yards) in the Gamecocks’ 45-9 victory over Towson in Week 2. In his career, Swain has five punt-return TDs, good for the South Carolina career record. Place-kicker Malik Orsan is 5 of 6 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 52 yards. Punter Mason Love is averaging 44.3 yards on 10 kicks, and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. away.headline: Georgia Southern turns to Sun Belt play after three straight losses
away.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Eagles open conference play at Coastal Carolina with a 1-3 record, plus key injury updates following Saturday’s loss to No. 25 Houston. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4. Georgia Southern and Coastal Carolina kick off Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. from Brooks Stadium in Conway, South Carolina. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the biggest ACC games of the season takes place Saturday night as No. 4 Miami heads to Death Valley to take on Clemson . Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Clemson vs. Miami scouting report Where Clemson has an advantage: Miami hasn't faced a secondary as good as Clemson's. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. picks.blurb: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Sam Navarro-Imagn Images; Ken Ruinard-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 1, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Canes and Tigers will have the eyes of the nation on them on Saturday night in a big game for two programs going in different directions. The Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers square off on Saturday night in Death Valley in a game with significant ACC title implications, with the game being shown in primetime on ABC. The Canes have surged to a 4-0 start, with only a slight flutter in the second half at Wake Forest after leading 31-7 being their only show of mortality thus far. Meanwhile, Clemson has improved to 3-1 after a season-opening 51-10 loss at LSU. Lifeless performances against Georgia Southern and in the first half against UNC have turned into a come from behind win over the Tar Heels and an impressive 24-10 win at Cal last weekend. Can the Tigers ride that modest improvement into an upset win on Saturday night? Our college football writers weighed in with their game predictions. Miami 38, Clemson 28 I think the writing is on the wall for Clemson and Dabo Swinney. The program is a shell of itself, esepcially from a talent acquisition standpoint. Things are the exact opposite for the Hurricanes, as they were less than 70 yards away from a national championship. Even so, I expect Clemson to show out for this game almost as a last ditch effort to save their season. It won't be enough, as the Hurricanes prove to be too explosive for the Tigers. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 30, Clemson 10 This game had the potential to be one of the better matchups in the ACC this season if Clemson held up their end of the bargain, but it looks like Dabo and the boys have only fallen further down the list in terms of program competence. The quarterback position is a mess, and a lot of the notable draft prospects heading into the season simply haven't played up to the offseason hype. On the other hand, you have a Miami team with not only one of the sport's most explosive weapons in Malachi Toney, but also one of the most efficient passers in college football in Darian Mensah. I know Clemson is at home, but this has a chance to be a route for the Hurricanes. Give me Miami, big. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 34, Clemson 21 This game is much closer than the final score suggests, with Clemson hanging around for a large portion of the afternoon. One of the biggest storylines will be how the Tigers handle Malachi Toney. It'll be interesting to see if Clemson allows CB Ashton Hampton to follow Toney around the field and essentially shadow him, considering Hampton is the most talented defensive back Miami has faced to this point. If Clemson can limit Toney and force Miami to win elsewhere, the Tigers have a chance to make this uncomfortable. Ultimately, though, Miami's overall talent takes over as the game progresses. The Hurricanes make enough explosive plays on offense to create separation, while Clemson capitalizes on a couple of coverage busts from the Miami secondary for some big plays of its own. Miami's depth and playmakers prove to be the difference in the second half, allowing the Hurricanes to pull away and finish with a 34-21 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Miami 30, Clemson 13 This feels like a game that could be closer than many pundits are giving it credit for, and perhaps those in Las Vegas as well. The 17-point line feels out of place for what Clemson has been over the last decade, but Dabo Swinney's Tigers have looked anything but the part of contenders the last few years. Clemson's secondary is talented, led by Ashton Hampton, who could play himself into first round consideration in April's NFL Draft. I could see the Tigers giving Miami's offense problems and preventing some of the chunk plays that Miami has ripped off all year with the exception of a quarter and a half against Wake Forest. But Clemson freshman QB Tait Reynolds is going to have a rough experience against a Miami team that's starting to get a tad healthier on the defensive side of the ball. DL Ahmad Moten, Sr. and Armondo Blount are off the injury report and appear set to be available on Saturday, along with CB Damari Brown. Starting CB Xavier Lucas could even possibly be in play, but even if not, Ethan O'Connor has been one of the better CBs in the ACC this year and can handle things very capably. Miami slowly puts this one away in the second half with Mark Fletcher, Jr., who is also off the injury report, pounding away in the fourth quarter on a tired defense. away.blurb: "I think our guys do a really good job being able to take, like, minor adjustments or little details, and as a staff, I think our guys do a really good job of helping out, hey, this is where maybe we got to clean something up, or maybe a better call in this situation might be this, and, you know, being able to react and respond, and then also understanding, like, hey, the play off of this is probably going to be this shot or this moving pocket or this a run that’s a little bit different where the scheme might fit a little bit different, a tweak here or there, and our guys can handle that pretty well," Hetherman said. "And I just think that’s our guys putting in the effort during the week, putting in the effort in the offseason to understand what’s happening when I’m blocking man away, blocking when I’m getting certain pictures in the box or out of the box, and understanding the game of football." After the Canes and Hetherman figure out what they like to do and lock them down. Some teams struggle to get past the 50-yard line, while Miami has its team ready to pin its back to attack and get after the quarterback. Miami's sack total might only be 10, but they are one of the best teams in the country at quarterback pressure. If the ball is not out within 2.5 seconds, other teams are at the mercy of the Hurricanes. CORAL GABLES, Fla. — Last season, the Miami Hurricanes spent time inside the top 10 of overall defense with the best pass-rushing duo in the country along with some of the best corner play in the country. Statistically , No. 4 Miami is better this season. Over four weeks, the Hurricanes rank as the No. 2 overall defense in the land, only behind No. 3 Notre Dame . They are the No. 4-ranked scoring defense but still have some areas to clean up, with sacks and turnovers starting to increase. But how is this possible with the Hurricanes missing their top two cornerbacks and best young linebackers on the roster? It's simple: defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman . Schemes and defensive adjustments are the calling card for Hetherman and this Hurricanes defense. The first drive of each Miami game, depending on the talent of the opposing offense, will likely get the first drive down the field and add some points to the board. The process is simple for Hetherman, and the defense changes. Learn, adjust, and adapt. It doesn't have to wait until the second half if something can be fixed quickly. Most times, those quick fixes are all it takes for the Hurricanes to get roaring. Moreover, with that mindset, the Hurricanes have only allowed four offensive touchdowns this season. One to start the season against Stanford, and the rest came against Wake Forest, who are better than most give them credit for. Miami's offense will get most of the praise as it should. Could the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes’ depleted secondary receive a boost when they play at the Clemson Tigers on Saturday night (7:30 p.m., ABC)? Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal on Monday said Lucas was “getting closer” to returning to game action. “Not all the way there yet,” Cristobal said. “Hopefully, good news later this week. There’s been a lot of progress. Works his butt off, but not all the way there.” In their absence, the trio of Ethan O’Connor, Damari Brown and safety Bryce Fitzgerald have been Miami’s primary outside cornerbacks. Speaking of Brown, he did not play last week against Central Michigan but does not have an injury designation, signaling that he should be good to go against Clemson.

As expected, sophomore tight end Luka Gilbert (undisclosed), redshirt junior running back CharMar “Marty” Brown (right knee), and sophomore wide receiver Joshua Moore (right shoulder) have been ruled out – the case for the rest of the season. Cornerbacks junior Romanas “OJ” Frederique Jr. (left shoulder) and Ja’Boree Antoine (undisclosed) are ruled out for the weekend. Both defenders are expected to return at a later portion of the regular season. Antoine has yet to play and Frederique Jr. has been sidelined since the first drive against Stanford. Newly added to the list, redshirt junior tight end Owen Ruskavich (undisclosed) has been ruled out. He’s logged a new collegiate career high, playing 26 snaps this season. Ruskavich didn’t appear in last Saturday’s 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium. Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas (undisclosed) is listed as questionable. Head coach Mario Cristobal described a return this weekend as “possibly.” Lucas will likely be a game-time decision. The Hurricanes’ secondary has run thin over the last three weeks; a return would add much-needed depth. Sophomore linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. (undisclosed) is listed as questionable. He has shown promising signs this season. Marcelin Jr. is one of nine Hurricanes defenders with at least 10 tackles, including three solos and seven assists, a tackle for loss, and a forced pressure. Clemson has starting junior left guard Elyjah Thurmon (undisclosed) as questionable. Meanwhile, junior nickelback Corian Gipson and fifth-year defensive tackle Devarrick Woods, who missed last Friday’s 24-10 win over Cal, aren’t listed.
